units.leftText: These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel,
units.rightText: The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel:

units.leftText: for gaining wisdom and discipline, for comprehending words of insight,
units.rightText: To know wisdom and instruction; To discern the words of understanding;

units.leftText: and for receiving instruction in wise living and in righteousness, justice, and equity.
units.rightText: To receive instruction in wise dealing, In righteousness and justice and equity;

units.leftText: To impart prudence to the simple and knowledge and discretion to the young,
units.rightText: To give prudence to the simple, To the young man knowledge and discretion:
leftNotes: 1:4 The Hebrew word rendered simple in Proverbs refers to one who is naive, without moral direction, or inclined to evil.

units.leftText: let the wise listen and gain instruction, and the discerning acquire wise counsel
units.rightText: That the wise man may hear, and increase in learning; And that the man of understanding may attain unto sound counsels:

units.leftText: by understanding the proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise.
units.rightText: To understand a proverb, and a figure, The words of the wise, and their dark sayings.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline. The Enticement of Sin
units.rightText: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of knowledge; But the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
leftNotes: 1:7 The Hebrew words rendered as fool in Proverbs denote one who is morally deficient.

units.leftText: Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.
units.rightText: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, And forsake not the law of thy mother:

units.leftText: For they are a garland of grace on your head and a pendant around your neck.
units.rightText: For they shall be a chaplet of grace unto thy head, And chains about thy neck.

units.leftText: My son, if sinners entice you, do not yield to them.
units.rightText: My son, if sinners entice thee, Consent thou not.

units.leftText: If they say, “Come along, let us lie in wait for blood, let us ambush the innocent without cause,
units.rightText: If they say, Come with us, Let us lay wait for blood; Let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause;

units.leftText: let us swallow them alive like Sheol, and whole like those descending into the Pit.
units.rightText: Let us swallow them up alive as Sheol, And whole, as those that go down into the pit;

units.leftText: We will find all manner of precious goods; we will fill our houses with plunder.
units.rightText: We shall find all precious substance; We shall fill our houses with spoil;

units.leftText: Throw in your lot with us; let us all share one purse” —
units.rightText: Thou shalt cast thy lot among us; We will all have one purse:

units.leftText: my son, do not walk the road with them or set foot upon their path.
units.rightText: My son, walk not thou in the way with them; Refrain thy foot from their path:

units.leftText: For their feet run to evil, and they are swift to shed blood.
units.rightText: For their feet run to evil, And they make haste to shed blood.

units.leftText: How futile it is to spread the net where any bird can see it!
units.rightText: For in vain is the net spread In the sight of any bird:

units.leftText: But they lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.
units.rightText: And these lay wait for their own blood; They lurk privily for their own lives.

units.leftText: Such is the fate of all who are greedy, whose unjust gain takes the lives of its possessors. Wisdom Calls Aloud
units.rightText: So are the ways of every one that is greedy of gain; It taketh away the life of the owners thereof.

units.leftText: Wisdom calls out in the street, she lifts her voice in the square;
units.rightText: Wisdom crieth aloud in the street; She uttereth her voice in the broad places;

units.leftText: in the main concourse she cries aloud, at the city gates she makes her speech:
units.rightText: She crieth in the chief place of concourse; At the entrance of the gates, In the city, she uttereth her words:
leftNotes: 1:21 Or from the top of the wall

units.leftText: “How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways? How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?
units.rightText: How long, ye simple ones, will ye love simplicity? And scoffers delight them in scoffing, And fools hate knowledge?

units.leftText: If you had repented at my rebuke, then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you; I would have made my words known to you.
units.rightText: Turn you at my reproof: Behold, I will pour out my spirit upon you; I will make known my words unto you.

units.leftText: Because you refused my call, and no one took my outstretched hand,
units.rightText: Because I have called, and ye have refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man hath regarded;

units.leftText: because you neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction,
units.rightText: But ye have set at nought all my counsel, And would none of my reproof:

units.leftText: in turn I will mock your calamity; I will sneer when terror strikes you,
units.rightText: I also will laugh in the day of your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh;

units.leftText: when your dread comes like a storm, and your destruction like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm you.
units.rightText: When your fear cometh as a storm, And your calamity cometh on as a whirlwind; When distress and anguish come upon you.

units.leftText: Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.
units.rightText: Then will they call upon me, but I will not answer; They will seek me diligently, but they shall not find me:

units.leftText: For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD.
units.rightText: For that they hated knowledge, And did not choose the fear of Jehovah,

units.leftText: They accepted none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof.
units.rightText: They would none of my counsel, They despised all my reproof.

units.leftText: So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.
units.rightText: Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way, And be filled with their own devices.

units.leftText: For the waywardness of the simple will slay them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.
units.rightText: For the backsliding of the simple shall slay them, And the careless ease of fools shall destroy them.

units.leftText: But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil.”
units.rightText: But whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell securely, And shall be quiet without fear of evil.

units.leftText: My son, if you accept my words and hide my commandments within you,
units.rightText: My son, if thou wilt receive my words, And lay up my commandments with thee;

units.leftText: if you incline your ear to wisdom and direct your heart to understanding,
units.rightText: So as to incline thine ear unto wisdom, And apply thy heart to understanding;

units.leftText: if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding,
units.rightText: Yea, if thou cry after discernment, And lift up thy voice for understanding;

units.leftText: if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure,
units.rightText: If thou seek her as silver, And search for her as for hid treasures:

units.leftText: then you will discern the fear of the LORD and discover the knowledge of God.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou understand the fear of Jehovah, And find the knowledge of God.

units.leftText: For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
units.rightText: For Jehovah giveth wisdom; Out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding:

units.leftText: He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield to those who walk with integrity,
units.rightText: He layeth up sound wisdom for the upright; He is a shield to them that walk in integrity;

units.leftText: to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints.
units.rightText: That he may guard the paths of justice, And preserve the way of his saints.

units.leftText: Then you will discern righteousness and justice and equity— every good path.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou understand righteousness and justice, And equity, yea, every good path.

units.leftText: For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul.
units.rightText: For wisdom shall enter into thy heart, And knowledge shall be pleasant unto thy soul;

units.leftText: Discretion will watch over you, and understanding will guard you,
units.rightText: Discretion shall watch over thee; Understanding shall keep thee:

units.leftText: to deliver you from the way of evil, from the man who speaks perversity,
units.rightText: To deliver thee from the way of evil, From the men that speak perverse things;

units.leftText: from those who leave the straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness,
units.rightText: Who forsake the paths of uprightness, To walk in the ways of darkness;

units.leftText: from those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the twistedness of evil,
units.rightText: Who rejoice to do evil, And delight in the perverseness of evil;

units.leftText: whose paths are crooked and whose ways are devious.
units.rightText: Who are crooked in their ways, And wayward in their paths:

units.leftText: It will rescue you from the forbidden woman, from the stranger with seductive words
units.rightText: To deliver thee from the strange woman, Even from the foreigner that flattereth with her words;
leftNotes: 2:16 Or wayward wife
2:16 Or adulteress

units.leftText: who abandons the partner of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God.
units.rightText: That forsaketh the friend of her youth, And forgetteth the covenant of her God:

units.leftText: For her house sinks down to death, and her tracks to the departed spirits.
units.rightText: For her house inclineth unto death, And her paths unto the dead;
leftNotes: 2:18 Hebrew to the Rephaim

units.leftText: None who go to her return or negotiate the paths of life.
units.rightText: None that go unto her return again, Neither do they attain unto the paths of life:

units.leftText: So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous.
units.rightText: That thou mayest walk in the way of good men, And keep the paths of the righteous.

units.leftText: For the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it;
units.rightText: For the upright shall dwell in the land, And the perfect shall remain in it.

units.leftText: but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be uprooted.
units.rightText: But the wicked shall be cut off from the land, And the treacherous shall be rooted out of it.

units.leftText: My son, do not forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments;
units.rightText: My son, forget not my law; But let thy heart keep my commandments:

units.leftText: for they will add length to your days, years and peace to your life.
units.rightText: For length of days, and years of life, And peace, will they add to thee.

units.leftText: Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
units.rightText: Let not kindness and truth forsake thee: Bind them about thy neck; Write them upon the tablet of thy heart:
leftNotes: 3:3 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Then you will find favor and high regard in the sight of God and man.
units.rightText: So shalt thou find favor and good understanding In the sight of God and man.

units.leftText: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding;
units.rightText: Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding:

units.leftText: in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.
units.rightText: In all thy ways acknowledge him, And he will direct thy paths.

units.leftText: Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
units.rightText: Be not wise in thine own eyes; Fear Jehovah, and depart from evil:

units.leftText: This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones.
units.rightText: It will be health to thy navel, And marrow to thy bones.
leftNotes: 3:8 Hebrew navel
3:8 Or medicine

units.leftText: Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your crops;
units.rightText: Honor Jehovah with thy substance, And with the first-fruits of all thine increase:

units.leftText: then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
units.rightText: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, And thy vats shall overflow with new wine.

units.leftText: My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, and do not loathe His rebuke;
units.rightText: My son, despise not the chastening of Jehovah; Neither be weary of his reproof:
leftNotes: 3:11 LXX and do not lose heart when He rebukes; cited in Hebrews 12:5|HEB 12:5*

units.leftText: for the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as does a father the son in whom he delights. The Blessings of Wisdom
units.rightText: For whom Jehovah loveth he reproveth, Even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.
leftNotes: 3:12 LXX and He flogs every son He receives; cited in Hebrews 12:6|HEB 12:6*

units.leftText: Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, the man who acquires understanding,
units.rightText: Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, And the man that getteth understanding.

units.leftText: for she is more profitable than silver, and her gain is better than fine gold.
units.rightText: For the gaining of it is better than the gaining of silver, And the profit thereof than fine gold.

units.leftText: She is more precious than rubies; nothing you desire compares with her.
units.rightText: She is more precious than rubies: And none of the things thou canst desire are to be compared unto her.

units.leftText: Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor.
units.rightText: Length of days is in her right hand; In her left hand are riches and honor.

units.leftText: All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful.
units.rightText: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, And all her paths are peace.

units.leftText: She is a tree of life to those who embrace her, and those who lay hold of her are blessed.
units.rightText: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: And happy is every one that retaineth her.

units.leftText: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding.
units.rightText: Jehovah by wisdom founded the earth; By understanding he established the heavens.

units.leftText: By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open, and the clouds dripped with dew.
units.rightText: By his knowledge the depths were broken up, And the skies drop down the dew.

units.leftText: My son, do not lose sight of this: Preserve sound judgment and discernment.
units.rightText: My son, let them not depart from thine eyes; Keep sound wisdom and discretion:

units.leftText: They will be life to your soul and adornment to your neck.
units.rightText: So shall they be life unto thy soul, And grace to thy neck.

units.leftText: Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble.
units.rightText: Then shalt thou walk in thy way securely, And thy foot shall not stumble.

units.leftText: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
units.rightText: When thou liest down, thou shalt not be afraid: Yea, thou shalt lie down, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

units.leftText: Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked,
units.rightText: Be not afraid of sudden fear, Neither of the desolation of the wicked, when it cometh:

units.leftText: for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from the snare.
units.rightText: For Jehovah will be thy confidence, And will keep thy foot from being taken.

units.leftText: Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act.
units.rightText: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, When it is in the power of thy hand to do it.
leftNotes: 3:27 Or from its owners

units.leftText: Do not tell your neighbor, “Come back tomorrow and I will provide”— when you already have the means.
units.rightText: Say not unto thy neighbor, Go, and come again, And to-morrow I will give; When thou hast it by thee.

units.leftText: Do not devise evil against your neighbor, for he trustfully dwells beside you.
units.rightText: Devise not evil against thy neighbor, Seeing he dwelleth securely by thee.

units.leftText: Do not accuse a man without cause, when he has done you no harm.
units.rightText: Strive not with a man without cause, If he have done thee no harm.

units.leftText: Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways;
units.rightText: Envy thou not the man of violence, And choose none of his ways.

units.leftText: for the LORD detests the perverse, but He is a friend to the upright.
units.rightText: For the perverse is an abomination to Jehovah; But his friendship is with the upright.

units.leftText: The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.
units.rightText: The curse of Jehovah is in the house of the wicked; But he blesseth the habitation of the righteous.

units.leftText: He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble.
units.rightText: Surely he scoffeth at the scoffers; But he giveth grace unto the lowly.
leftNotes: 3:34 LXX The Lord opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble; cited in James 4:6|JAS 4:6* and 1 Peter 5:5

units.leftText: The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame.
units.rightText: The wise shall inherit glory; But shame shall be the promotion of fools.

units.leftText: Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction; pay attention and gain understanding.
units.rightText: Hear, my sons, the instruction of a father, And attend to know understanding:

units.leftText: For I give you sound teaching; do not abandon my directive.
units.rightText: For I give you good doctrine; Forsake ye not my law.

units.leftText: When I was a son to my father, tender and the only child of my mother,
units.rightText: For I was a son unto my father, Tender and only beloved in the sight of my mother.

units.leftText: he taught me and said, “Let your heart lay hold of my words; keep my commands and you will live.
units.rightText: And he taught me, and said unto me: Let thy heart retain my words; Keep my commandments, and live;

units.leftText: Get wisdom, get understanding; do not forget my words or turn from them.
units.rightText: Get wisdom, get understanding; Forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth;

units.leftText: Do not forsake wisdom, and she will preserve you; love her, and she will guard you.
units.rightText: Forsake her not, and she will preserve thee; Love her, and she will keep thee.

units.leftText: Wisdom is supreme; so acquire wisdom. And whatever you may acquire, gain understanding.
units.rightText: Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom; Yea, with all thy getting get understanding.
leftNotes: 4:7 Or And whatever else you acquire

units.leftText: Prize her, and she will exalt you; if you embrace her, she will honor you.
units.rightText: Exalt her, and she will promote thee; She will bring thee to honor, when thou dost embrace her.

units.leftText: She will set a garland of grace on your head; she will present you with a crown of beauty.”
units.rightText: She will give to thy head a chaplet of grace; A crown of beauty will she deliver to thee.

units.leftText: Listen, my son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will be many.
units.rightText: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings; And the years of thy life shall be many.

units.leftText: I will guide you in the way of wisdom; I will lead you on straight paths.
units.rightText: I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in paths of uprightness.

units.leftText: When you walk, your steps will not be impeded; when you run, you will not stumble.
units.rightText: When thou goest, thy steps shall not be straitened; And if thou runnest, thou shalt not stumble.

units.leftText: Hold on to instruction; do not let go. Guard it, for it is your life.
units.rightText: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: Keep her; for she is thy life.

units.leftText: Do not set foot on the path of the wicked or walk in the way of evildoers.
units.rightText: Enter not into the path of the wicked, And walk not in the way of evil men.

units.leftText: Avoid it; do not travel on it. Turn from it and pass on by.
units.rightText: Avoid it, pass not by it; Turn from it, and pass on.

units.leftText: For they cannot sleep unless they do evil; they are deprived of slumber until they make someone fall.
units.rightText: For they sleep not, except they do evil; And their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall.

units.leftText: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
units.rightText: For they eat the bread of wickedness, And drink the wine of violence.

units.leftText: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.
units.rightText: But the path of the righteous is as the dawning light, That shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

units.leftText: But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble.
units.rightText: The way of the wicked is as darkness: They know not at what they stumble.

units.leftText: My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
units.rightText: My son, attend to my words; Incline thine ear unto my sayings.

units.leftText: Do not lose sight of them; keep them within your heart.
units.rightText: Let them not depart from thine eyes; Keep them in the midst of thy heart.

units.leftText: For they are life to those who find them, and health to the whole body.
units.rightText: For they are life unto those that find them, And health to all their flesh.

units.leftText: Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life.
units.rightText: Keep thy heart with all diligence; For out of it are the issues of life.

units.leftText: Put away deception from your mouth; keep your lips from perverse speech.
units.rightText: Put away from thee a wayward mouth, And perverse lips put far from thee.

units.leftText: Let your eyes look forward; fix your gaze straight ahead.
units.rightText: Let thine eyes look right on, And let thine eyelids look straight before thee.

units.leftText: Make a level path for your feet, and all your ways will be sure.
units.rightText: Make level the path of thy feet, And let all thy ways be established.
leftNotes: 4:26 Or Ponder the path for your feet; LXX Make straight paths for your feet; cited in Hebrews 12:13|HEB 12:13*

units.leftText: Do not swerve to the right or to the left; turn your feet away from evil.
units.rightText: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: Remove thy foot from evil.

units.leftText: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my insight,
units.rightText: My son, attend unto my wisdom; Incline thine ear to my understanding:

units.leftText: that you may maintain discretion and your lips may preserve knowledge.
units.rightText: That thou mayest preserve discretion, And that thy lips may keep knowledge.

units.leftText: Though the lips of the forbidden woman drip honey and her speech is smoother than oil,
units.rightText: For the lips of a strange woman drop honey, And her mouth is smoother than oil:
leftNotes: 5:3 Or the adulteress
5:3 Or her palate

units.leftText: in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.
units.rightText: But in the end she is bitter as wormwood, Sharp as a two-edged sword.

units.leftText: Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to Sheol.
units.rightText: Her feet go down to death; Her steps take hold on Sheol;
leftNotes: 5:5 Or lay hold of Sheol

units.leftText: She does not consider the path of life; she does not know that her ways are unstable.
units.rightText: So that she findeth not the level path of life: Her ways are unstable, and she knoweth it not.

units.leftText: So now, my sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: Now therefore, my sons, hearken unto me, And depart not from the words of my mouth.

units.leftText: Keep your path far from her; do not go near the door of her house,
units.rightText: Remove thy way far from her, And come not nigh the door of her house;

units.leftText: lest you concede your vigor to others, and your years to one who is cruel;
units.rightText: Lest thou give thine honor unto others, And thy years unto the cruel;

units.leftText: lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labors enrich the house of a foreigner.
units.rightText: Lest strangers be filled with thy strength, And thy labors be in the house of an alien,

units.leftText: At the end of your life you will groan when your flesh and your body are spent,
units.rightText: And thou mourn at thy latter end, When thy flesh and thy body are consumed,

units.leftText: and you will say, “How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof!
units.rightText: And say, How have I hated instruction, And my heart despised reproof;

units.leftText: I did not listen to the voice of my teachers or incline my ear to my mentors.
units.rightText: Neither have I obeyed the voice of my teachers, Nor inclined mine ear to them that instructed me!

units.leftText: I am on the brink of utter ruin in the midst of the whole assembly.”
units.rightText: I was well-nigh in all evil In the midst of the assembly and congregation.

units.leftText: Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well.
units.rightText: Drink waters out of thine own cistern, And running waters out of thine own well.

units.leftText: Why should your springs flow in the streets, your streams of water in the public squares?
units.rightText: Should thy springs be dispersed abroad, And streams of water in the streets?

units.leftText: Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers.
units.rightText: Let them be for thyself alone, And not for strangers with thee.

units.leftText: May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth:
units.rightText: Let thy fountain be blessed; And rejoice in the wife of thy youth.

units.leftText: A loving doe, a graceful fawn— may her breasts satisfy you always; may you be captivated by her love forever.
units.rightText: As a loving hind and a pleasant doe, Let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; And be thou ravished always with her love.
leftNotes: 5:19 Or be led astray; also in verse 20

units.leftText: Why be captivated, my son, by an adulteress, or embrace the bosom of a stranger?
units.rightText: For why shouldest thou, my son, be ravished with a strange woman, And embrace the bosom of a foreigner?
leftNotes: 5:20 Or a foreign woman or another man’s wife

units.leftText: For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.
units.rightText: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Jehovah; And he maketh level all his paths.
leftNotes: 5:21 Or ponders or makes level

units.leftText: The iniquities of a wicked man entrap him; the cords of his sin entangle him.
units.rightText: His own iniquities shall take the wicked, And he shall be holden with the cords of his sin.

units.leftText: He dies for lack of discipline, led astray by his own great folly.
units.rightText: He shall die for lack of instruction; And in the greatness of his folly he shall go astray.

units.leftText: My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have struck hands in pledge with a stranger,
units.rightText: My son, if thou art become surety for thy neighbor, If thou hast stricken thy hands for a stranger;

units.leftText: if you have been trapped by the words of your lips, ensnared by the words of your mouth,
units.rightText: Thou art snared with the words of thy mouth, Thou art taken with the words of thy mouth.

units.leftText: then do this, my son, to free yourself, for you have fallen into your neighbor’s hands: Go, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor.
units.rightText: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself, Seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbor: Go, humble thyself, and importune thy neighbor;
leftNotes: 6:3 Or hasten

units.leftText: Allow no sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.
units.rightText: Give not sleep to thine eyes, Nor slumber to thine eyelids;

units.leftText: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
units.rightText: Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand of the hunter, And as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
leftNotes: 6:5 Hebrew does not include of the hunter.

units.leftText: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise.
units.rightText: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; Consider her ways, and be wise:

units.leftText: Without a commander, without an overseer or ruler,
units.rightText: Which having no chief, Overseer, or ruler,

units.leftText: it prepares its provisions in summer; it gathers its food at harvest.
units.rightText: Provideth her bread in the summer, And gathereth her food in the harvest.

units.leftText: How long will you lie there, O slacker? When will you get up from your sleep?
units.rightText: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? When wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?

units.leftText: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
units.rightText: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep:

units.leftText: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
units.rightText: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.

units.leftText: A worthless person, a wicked man, walks with a perverse mouth,
units.rightText: A worthless person, a man of iniquity, Is he that walketh with a perverse mouth;

units.leftText: winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, and pointing with his fingers.
units.rightText: That winketh with his eyes, that speaketh with his feet, That maketh signs with his fingers;

units.leftText: With deceit in his heart he devises evil; he continually sows discord.
units.rightText: In whose heart is perverseness, Who deviseth evil continually, Who soweth discord.

units.leftText: Therefore calamity will come upon him suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered beyond recovery.
units.rightText: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly; On a sudden shall he be broken, and that without remedy.

units.leftText: There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him:
units.rightText: There are six things which Jehovah hateth; Yea, seven which are an abomination unto him:

units.leftText: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
units.rightText: Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, And hands that shed innocent blood;

units.leftText: a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that run swiftly to evil,
units.rightText: A heart that deviseth wicked purposes, Feet that are swift in running to mischief,

units.leftText: a false witness who gives false testimony, and one who stirs up discord among brothers. Warnings against Adultery
units.rightText: A false witness that uttereth lies, And he that soweth discord among brethren.

units.leftText: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.
units.rightText: My son, keep the commandment of thy father, And forsake not the law of thy mother:

units.leftText: Bind them always upon your heart; tie them around your neck.
units.rightText: Bind them continually upon thy heart; Tie them about thy neck.

units.leftText: When you walk, they will guide you; when you lie down, they will watch over you; when you awake, they will speak to you.
units.rightText: When thou walkest, it shall lead thee; When thou sleepest, it shall watch over thee; And when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.

units.leftText: For this commandment is a lamp, this teaching is a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way to life,
units.rightText: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; And reproofs of instruction are the way of life:

units.leftText: to keep you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the adulteress.
units.rightText: To keep thee from the evil woman, From the flattery of the foreigner’s tongue.
leftNotes: 6:24 Or the stranger

units.leftText: Do not lust in your heart for her beauty or let her captivate you with her eyes.
units.rightText: Lust not after her beauty in thy heart; Neither let her take thee with her eyelids.
leftNotes: 6:25 Or eyelids or eyelashes

units.leftText: For the levy of the prostitute is poverty, and the adulteress preys upon your very life.
units.rightText: For on account of a harlot a man is brought to a piece of bread; And the adulteress hunteth for the precious life.
leftNotes: 6:26 Literally a crust of bread

units.leftText: Can a man embrace fire and his clothes not be burned?
units.rightText: Can a man take fire in his bosom, And his clothes not be burned?

units.leftText: Can a man walk on hot coals without scorching his feet?
units.rightText: Or can one walk upon hot coals, And his feet not be scorched?

units.leftText: So is he who sleeps with another man’s wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.
units.rightText: So he that goeth in to his neighbor’s wife; Whosoever toucheth her shall not be unpunished.

units.leftText: Men do not despise the thief if he steals to satisfy his hunger.
units.rightText: Men do not despise a thief, if he steal To satisfy himself when he is hungry:

units.leftText: Yet if caught, he must pay sevenfold; he must give up all the wealth of his house.
units.rightText: But if he be found, he shall restore sevenfold; He shall give all the substance of his house.

units.leftText: He who commits adultery lacks judgment; whoever does so destroys himself.
units.rightText: He that committeth adultery with a woman is void of understanding: He doeth it who would destroy his own soul.

units.leftText: Wounds and dishonor will befall him, and his reproach will never be wiped away.
units.rightText: Wounds and dishonor shall he get; And his reproach shall not be wiped away.

units.leftText: For jealousy enrages a husband, and he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance.
units.rightText: For jealousy is the rage of a man; And he will not spare in the day of vengeance.

units.leftText: He will not be appeased by any ransom, or persuaded by lavish gifts.
units.rightText: He will not regard any ransom; Neither will he rest content, though thou givest many gifts.

units.leftText: My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you.
units.rightText: My son, keep my words, And lay up my commandments with thee.

units.leftText: Keep my commandments and live; guard my teachings as the apple of your eye.
units.rightText: Keep my commandments and live; And my law as the apple of thine eye.
leftNotes: 7:2 Literally the pupil

units.leftText: Tie them to your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
units.rightText: Bind them upon thy fingers; Write them upon the tablet of thy heart.

units.leftText: Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,” and call understanding your kinsman,
units.rightText: Say unto wisdom, Thou art my sister; And call understanding thy kinswoman:

units.leftText: that they may keep you from the adulteress, from the stranger with seductive words.
units.rightText: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, From the foreigner that flattereth with her words.

units.leftText: For at the window of my house I looked through the lattice.
units.rightText: For at the window of my house I looked forth through my lattice;

units.leftText: I saw among the simple, I noticed among the youths, a young man lacking judgment,
units.rightText: And I beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, A young man void of understanding,

units.leftText: crossing the street near her corner, strolling down the road to her house,
units.rightText: Passing through the street near her corner; And he went the way to her house,

units.leftText: at twilight, as the day was fading into the dark of the night.
units.rightText: In the twilight, in the evening of the day, In the middle of the night and in the darkness.

units.leftText: Then a woman came out to meet him, with the attire of a harlot and cunning of heart.
units.rightText: And, behold, there met him a woman With the attire of a harlot, and wily of heart.

units.leftText: She is loud and defiant; her feet do not remain at home.
units.rightText: (She is clamorous and wilful; Her feet abide not in her house:

units.leftText: Now in the street, now in the squares, she lurks at every corner.
units.rightText: Now she is in the streets, now in the broad places, And lieth in wait at every corner.)

units.leftText: She seizes him and kisses him; she brazenly says to him:
units.rightText: So she caught him, and kissed him, And with an impudent face she said unto him:

units.leftText: “I have made my peace offerings; today I have paid my vows.
units.rightText: Sacrifices of peace-offerings are with me; This day have I paid my vows.

units.leftText: So I came out to meet you; I sought you, and I have found you.
units.rightText: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, Diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee.

units.leftText: I have decked my bed with coverings, with colored linen from Egypt.
units.rightText: I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, With striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt.

units.leftText: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, with aloes, and with cinnamon.
units.rightText: I have perfumed my bed With myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

units.leftText: Come, let us take our fill of love till morning. Let us delight in loving caresses!
units.rightText: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning; Let us solace ourselves with loves.

units.leftText: For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
units.rightText: For the man is not at home; He is gone a long journey:

units.leftText: He took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.”
units.rightText: He hath taken a bag of money with him; He will come home at the full moon.

units.leftText: With her great persuasion she entices him; with her flattering lips she lures him.
units.rightText: With her much fair speech she causeth him to yield; With the flattering of her lips she forceth him along.

units.leftText: He follows her on impulse, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a deer bounding into a trap,
units.rightText: He goeth after her straightway, As an ox goeth to the slaughter, Or as one in fetters to the correction of the fool;
leftNotes: 7:22 Probable reading (see LXX, Vulgate, Syriac); Hebrew like fetters to discipline a fool

units.leftText: until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare— not knowing it will cost him his life.
units.rightText: Till an arrow strike through his liver; As a bird hasteth to the snare, And knoweth not that it is for his life.

units.leftText: Now, my sons, listen to me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
units.rightText: Now therefore, my sons, hearken unto me, And attend to the words of my mouth.

units.leftText: Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.
units.rightText: Let not thy heart decline to her ways; Go not astray in her paths.

units.leftText: For she has brought many down to death; her slain are many in number.
units.rightText: For she hath cast down many wounded: Yea, all her slain are a mighty host.

units.leftText: Her house is the road to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.
units.rightText: Her house is the way to Sheol, Going down to the chambers of death.

units.leftText: Does not wisdom call out, and understanding raise her voice?
units.rightText: Doth not wisdom cry, And understanding put forth her voice?

units.leftText: On the heights overlooking the road, at the crossroads she takes her stand.
units.rightText: On the top of high places by the way, Where the paths meet, she standeth;

units.leftText: Beside the gates to the city, at the entrances she cries out:
units.rightText: Beside the gates, at the entry of the city, At the coming in at the doors, she crieth aloud:

units.leftText: “To you, O men, I call out, and my cry is to the sons of men.
units.rightText: Unto you, O men, I call; And my voice is to the sons of men.

units.leftText: O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding.
units.rightText: O ye simple, understand prudence; And, ye fools, be of an understanding heart.
leftNotes: 8:5 Or instruct your minds

units.leftText: Listen, for I speak of noble things, and the opening of my lips will reveal right.
units.rightText: Hear, for I will speak excellent things; And the opening of my lips shall be right things.

units.leftText: For my mouth will speak the truth, and wickedness is detestable to my lips.
units.rightText: For my mouth shall utter truth; And wickedness is an abomination to my lips.

units.leftText: All the words of my mouth are righteous; none are crooked or perverse.
units.rightText: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.

units.leftText: They are all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge.
units.rightText: They are all plain to him that understandeth, And right to them that find knowledge.

units.leftText: Receive my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than pure gold.
units.rightText: Receive my instruction, and not silver; And knowledge rather than choice gold.

units.leftText: For wisdom is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire compares with her.
units.rightText: For wisdom is better than rubies; And all the things that may be desired are not to be compared unto it.

units.leftText: I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.
units.rightText: I wisdom have made prudence my dwelling, And find out knowledge and discretion.

units.leftText: To fear the LORD is to hate evil; I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech.
units.rightText: The fear of Jehovah is to hate evil: Pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, And the perverse mouth, do I hate.

units.leftText: Counsel and sound judgment are mine; I have insight and strength.
units.rightText: Counsel is mine, and sound knowledge: I am understanding; I have might.

units.leftText: By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws;
units.rightText: By me kings reign, And princes decree justice.

units.leftText: By me princes rule, and all nobles who govern justly.
units.rightText: By me princes rule, And nobles, even all the judges of the earth.
leftNotes: 8:16 Some Hebrew manuscripts and LXX who govern the earth

units.leftText: I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me.
units.rightText: I love them that love me; And those that seek me diligently shall find me.

units.leftText: With me are riches and honor, enduring wealth and righteousness.
units.rightText: Riches and honor are with me; Yea, durable wealth and righteousness.

units.leftText: My fruit is better than gold, pure gold, and my harvest surpasses choice silver.
units.rightText: My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; And my revenue than choice silver.

units.leftText: I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice,
units.rightText: I walk in the way of righteousness, In the midst of the paths of justice;

units.leftText: bestowing wealth on those who love me and making their treasuries full.
units.rightText: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance, And that I may fill their treasuries.

units.leftText: The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.
units.rightText: Jehovah possessed me in the beginning of his way, Before his works of old.
leftNotes: 8:22 Or The LORD possessed me at the beginning of His way

units.leftText: From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began.
units.rightText: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, Before the earth was.

units.leftText: When there were no watery depths, I was brought forth, when no springs were overflowing with water.
units.rightText: When there were no depths, I was brought forth, When there were no fountains abounding with water.

units.leftText: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth,
units.rightText: Before the mountains were settled, Before the hills was I brought forth;

units.leftText: before He made the land or fields, or any of the dust of the earth.
units.rightText: While as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, Nor the beginning of the dust of the world.

units.leftText: I was there when He established the heavens, when He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,
units.rightText: When he established the heavens, I was there: When he set a circle upon the face of the deep,

units.leftText: when He established the clouds above, when the fountains of the deep gushed forth,
units.rightText: When he made firm the skies above, When the fountains of the deep became strong,

units.leftText: when He set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command, when He marked out the foundations of the earth.
units.rightText: When he gave to the sea its bound, That the waters should not transgress his commandment, When he marked out the foundations of the earth;

units.leftText: Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day, rejoicing always in His presence.
units.rightText: Then I was by him, as a master workman; And I was daily his delight, Rejoicing always before him,
leftNotes: 8:30 Or filled with His delight

units.leftText: I was rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men.
units.rightText: Rejoicing in his habitable earth; And my delight was with the sons of men.

units.leftText: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
units.rightText: Now therefore, my sons, hearken unto me; For blessed are they that keep my ways.

units.leftText: Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it.
units.rightText: Hear instruction, and be wise, And refuse it not.

units.leftText: Blessed is the man who listens to me, watching daily at my doors, waiting at the posts of my doorway.
units.rightText: Blessed is the man that heareth me, Watching daily at my gates, Waiting at the posts of my doors.

units.leftText: For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD.
units.rightText: For whoso findeth me findeth life, And shall obtain favor of Jehovah.

units.leftText: But he who fails to find me harms himself; all who hate me love death.”
units.rightText: But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul: All they that hate me love death.

units.leftText: Wisdom has built her house; she has carved out her seven pillars.
units.rightText: Wisdom hath builded her house; She hath hewn out her seven pillars:
leftNotes: 9:1 Hebrew; LXX, Syriac, and Aramaic Targum has set up

units.leftText: She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine; she has also set her table.
units.rightText: She hath killed her beasts; she hath mingled her wine; She hath also furnished her table:

units.leftText: She has sent out her maidservants; she calls out from the heights of the city.
units.rightText: She hath sent forth her maidens; She crieth upon the highest places of the city:

units.leftText: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.
units.rightText: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither: As for him that is void of understanding, she saith to him,

units.leftText: “Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
units.rightText: Come, eat ye of my bread, And drink of the wine which I have mingled.

units.leftText: Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.”
units.rightText: Leave off, ye simple ones, and live; And walk in the way of understanding.

units.leftText: He who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself; he who rebukes a wicked man taints himself.
units.rightText: He that correcteth a scoffer getteth to himself reviling; And he that reproveth a wicked man getteth himself a blot.

units.leftText: Do not rebuke a mocker, or he will hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.
units.rightText: Reprove not a scoffer, lest he hate thee: Reprove a wise man, and he will love thee.

units.leftText: Instruct a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will increase his learning.
units.rightText: Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
units.rightText: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom; And the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.

units.leftText: For through wisdom your days will be multiplied, and years will be added to your life.
units.rightText: For by me thy days shall be multiplied, And the years of thy life shall be increased.
leftNotes: 9:11 LXX, Syriac, and Aramaic Targum; Hebrew through me

units.leftText: If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage; but if you scoff, you alone will bear the consequences. The Way of Folly
units.rightText: If thou art wise, thou art wise for thyself; And if thou scoffest, thou alone shalt bear it.

units.leftText: The woman named Folly is loud; she is naive and knows nothing.
units.rightText: The foolish woman is clamorous; She is simple, and knoweth nothing.

units.leftText: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the heights of the city,
units.rightText: And she sitteth at the door of her house, On a seat in the high places of the city,

units.leftText: calling out to those who pass by, who make their paths straight.
units.rightText: To call to them that pass by, Who go right on their ways:

units.leftText: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.
units.rightText: Whoso is simple, let him turn in hither; And as for him that is void of understanding, she saith to him,

units.leftText: “Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is tasty!”
units.rightText: Stolen waters are sweet, And bread eaten in secret is pleasant.

units.leftText: But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
units.rightText: But he knoweth not that the dead are there; That her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
leftNotes: 9:18 Hebrew the Rephaim

units.leftText: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.
units.rightText: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son maketh a glad father; But a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother.

units.leftText: Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
units.rightText: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing; But righteousness delivereth from death.

units.leftText: The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked.
units.rightText: Jehovah will not suffer the soul of the righteous to famish; But he thrusteth away the desire of the wicked.

units.leftText: Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.
units.rightText: He becometh poor that worketh with a slack hand; But the hand of the diligent maketh rich.

units.leftText: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during harvest is a disgraceful son.
units.rightText: He that gathereth in summer is a wise son; But he that sleepeth in harvest is a son that causeth shame.

units.leftText: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
units.rightText: Blessings are upon the head of the righteous; But violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.
leftNotes: 10:6 Or but violence covers the mouth of the wicked; also in verse 11

units.leftText: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
units.rightText: The memory of the righteous is blessed; But the name of the wicked shall rot.

units.leftText: A wise heart will receive commandments, but foolish lips will come to ruin.
units.rightText: The wise in heart will receive commandments; But a prating fool shall fall.

units.leftText: He who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
units.rightText: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely; But he that perverteth his ways shall be known.

units.leftText: He who winks the eye causes grief, and foolish lips will come to ruin.
units.rightText: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow; But a prating fool shall fall.
leftNotes: 10:10 Or babbling fools will fall

units.leftText: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
units.rightText: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life; But violence covereth the mouth of the wicked.

units.leftText: Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions.
units.rightText: Hatred stirreth up strifes; But love covereth all transgressions.
leftNotes: 10:12 See 1 Peter 4:8|1PE 4:8*

units.leftText: Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the back of him who lacks judgment.
units.rightText: In the lips of him that hath discernment wisdom is found; But a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding.

units.leftText: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.
units.rightText: Wise men lay up knowledge; But the mouth of the foolish is a present destruction.

units.leftText: The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor.
units.rightText: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city: The destruction of the poor is their poverty.

units.leftText: The labor of the righteous leads to life, but the gain of the wicked brings punishment.
units.rightText: The labor of the righteous tendeth to life; The increase of the wicked, to sin.

units.leftText: Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray.
units.rightText: He is in the way of life that heedeth correction; But he that forsaketh reproof erreth.

units.leftText: The one who conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool.
units.rightText: He that hideth hatred is of lying lips; And he that uttereth a slander is a fool.

units.leftText: When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
units.rightText: In the multitude of words there wanteth not transgression; But he that refraineth his lips doeth wisely.

units.leftText: The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked has little worth.
units.rightText: The tongue of the righteous is as choice silver: The heart of the wicked is little worth.

units.leftText: The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment.
units.rightText: The lips of the righteous feed many; But the foolish die for lack of understanding.

units.leftText: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.
units.rightText: The blessing of Jehovah, it maketh rich; And he addeth no sorrow therewith.

units.leftText: The fool delights in shameful conduct, but a man of understanding has wisdom.
units.rightText: It is as sport to a fool to do wickedness; And so is wisdom to a man of understanding.

units.leftText: What the wicked man dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
units.rightText: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him; And the desire of the righteous shall be granted.

units.leftText: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, but the righteous are secure forever.
units.rightText: When the whirlwind passeth, the wicked is no more; But the righteous is an everlasting foundation.

units.leftText: Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the slacker to those who send him.
units.rightText: As vinegar to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, So is the sluggard to them that send him.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
units.rightText: The fear of Jehovah prolongeth days; But the years of the wicked shall be shortened.

units.leftText: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.
units.rightText: The hope of the righteous shall be gladness; But the expectation of the wicked shall perish.

units.leftText: The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright, but destruction awaits those who do evil.
units.rightText: The way of Jehovah is a stronghold to the upright; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.

units.leftText: The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not inhabit the land.
units.rightText: The righteous shall never be removed; But the wicked shall not dwell in the land.

units.leftText: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out.
units.rightText: The mouth of the righteous bringeth forth wisdom; But the perverse tongue shall be cut off.

units.leftText: The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
units.rightText: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable; But the mouth of the wicked speaketh perverseness.

units.leftText: Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight.
units.rightText: A false balance is an abomination to Jehovah; But a just weight is his delight.

units.leftText: When pride comes, disgrace follows, but with humility comes wisdom.
units.rightText: When pride cometh, then cometh shame; But with the lowly is wisdom.

units.leftText: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.
units.rightText: The integrity of the upright shall guide them; But the perverseness of the treacherous shall destroy them.

units.leftText: Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
units.rightText: Riches profit not in the day of wrath; But righteousness delivereth from death.

units.leftText: The righteousness of the blameless directs their path, but the wicked fall by their own wickedness.
units.rightText: The righteousness of the perfect shall direct his way; But the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness.

units.leftText: The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the faithless are trapped by their own desires.
units.rightText: The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them; But the treacherous shall be taken in their own iniquity.

units.leftText: When the wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of his strength vanishes.
units.rightText: When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish; And the hope of iniquity perisheth.

units.leftText: The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.
units.rightText: The righteous is delivered out of trouble; And the wicked cometh in his stead.

units.leftText: With his mouth the ungodly man destroys his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.
units.rightText: With his mouth the godless man destroyeth his neighbor; But through knowledge shall the righteous be delivered.

units.leftText: When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.
units.rightText: When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth; And when the wicked perish, there is shouting.

units.leftText: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
units.rightText: By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted; But it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.

units.leftText: Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment, but a man of understanding remains silent.
units.rightText: He that despiseth his neighbor is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding holdeth his peace.

units.leftText: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
units.rightText: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; But he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth a matter.

units.leftText: For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.
units.rightText: Where no wise guidance is, the people falleth; But in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

units.leftText: He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.
units.rightText: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it; But he that hateth suretyship is secure.

units.leftText: A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.
units.rightText: A gracious woman obtaineth honor; And violent men obtain riches.

units.leftText: A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.
units.rightText: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul; But he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh.

units.leftText: The wicked man earns an empty wage, but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.
units.rightText: The wicked earneth deceitful wages; But he that soweth righteousness hath a sure reward.

units.leftText: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death.
units.rightText: He that is stedfast in righteousness shall attain unto life; And he that pursueth evil doeth it to his own death.

units.leftText: The perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but the blameless in their walk are His delight.
units.rightText: They that are perverse in heart are an abomination to Jehovah; But such as are perfect in their way are his delight.

units.leftText: Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.
units.rightText: Though hand join in hand, the evil man shall not be unpunished; But the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

units.leftText: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
units.rightText: As a ring of gold in a swine’s snout, So is a fair woman that is without discretion.

units.leftText: The desire of the righteous leads only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings wrath.
units.rightText: The desire of the righteous is only good; But the expectation of the wicked is wrath.

units.leftText: One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.
units.rightText: There is that scattereth, and increaseth yet more; And there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth only to want.

units.leftText: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
units.rightText: The liberal soul shall be made fat; And he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

units.leftText: The people will curse the hoarder of grain, but blessing will crown the one who sells it.
units.rightText: He that withholdeth grain, the people shall curse him; But blessing shall be upon the head of him that selleth it.

units.leftText: He who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it.
units.rightText: He that diligently seeketh good seeketh favor; But he that searcheth after evil, it shall come unto him.

units.leftText: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage.
units.rightText: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall; But the righteous shall flourish as the green leaf.

units.leftText: He who brings trouble on his house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
units.rightText: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind; And the foolish shall be servant to the wise of heart.

units.leftText: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.
units.rightText: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life; And he that is wise winneth souls.

units.leftText: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
units.rightText: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth; How much more the wicked and the sinner!
leftNotes: 11:31 LXX If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?Cited in 1 Peter 4:18|1PE 4:18*

units.leftText: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid.
units.rightText: Whoso loveth correction loveth knowledge; But he that hateth reproof is brutish.

units.leftText: The good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a man who devises evil.
units.rightText: A good man shall obtain favor of Jehovah; But a man of wicked devices will he condemn.

units.leftText: A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.
units.rightText: A man shall not be established by wickedness; But the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

units.leftText: A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown, but she who causes shame is like decay in his bones.
units.rightText: A worthy woman is the crown of her husband; But she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.

units.leftText: The plans of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked leads to deceit.
units.rightText: The thoughts of the righteous are just; But the counsels of the wicked are deceit.

units.leftText: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
units.rightText: The words of the wicked are of lying in wait for blood; But the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.

units.leftText: The wicked are overthrown and perish, but the house of the righteous will stand.
units.rightText: The wicked are overthrown, and are not; But the house of the righteous shall stand.

units.leftText: A man is praised according to his wisdom, but a twisted mind is despised.
units.rightText: A man shall be commended according to his wisdom; But he that is of a perverse heart shall be despised.

units.leftText: Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food.
units.rightText: Better is he that is lightly esteemed, and hath a servant, Than he that honoreth himself, and lacketh bread.

units.leftText: A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty.
units.rightText: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast; But the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.

units.leftText: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment.
units.rightText: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain persons is void of understanding.

units.leftText: The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
units.rightText: The wicked desireth the net of evil men; But the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit.

units.leftText: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.
units.rightText: In the transgression of the lips is a snare to the evil man; But the righteous shall come out of trouble.

units.leftText: By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands returns to him.
units.rightText: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth; And the doings of a man’s hands shall be rendered unto him.

units.leftText: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel.
units.rightText: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes; But he that is wise hearkeneth unto counsel.

units.leftText: A fool’s anger is known at once, but a prudent man overlooks an insult.
units.rightText: A fool’s vexation is presently known; But a prudent man concealeth shame.

units.leftText: He who speaks the truth declares what is right, but a false witness speaks deceit.
units.rightText: He that uttereth truth showeth forth righteousness; But a false witness, deceit.

units.leftText: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
units.rightText: There is that speaketh rashly like the piercings of a sword; But the tongue of the wise is health.

units.leftText: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
units.rightText: The lip of truth shall be established for ever; But a lying tongue is but for a moment.

units.leftText: Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but the counselors of peace have joy.
units.rightText: Deceit is in the heart of them that devise evil; But to the counsellors of peace is joy.

units.leftText: No harm befalls the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.
units.rightText: There shall no mischief happen to the righteous; But the wicked shall be filled with evil.

units.leftText: Lying lips are detestable to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight.
units.rightText: Lying lips are an abomination to Jehovah; But they that deal truly are his delight.

units.leftText: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, but a foolish heart proclaims its folly.
units.rightText: A prudent man concealeth knowledge; But the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness.

units.leftText: The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
units.rightText: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule; But the slothful shall be put under taskwork.

units.leftText: Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up.
units.rightText: Heaviness in the heart of a man maketh it stoop; But a good word maketh it glad.

units.leftText: A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the ways of the wicked lead them astray.
units.rightText: The righteous is a guide to his neighbor; But the way of the wicked causeth them to err.

units.leftText: A lazy man does not roast his game, but a diligent man prizes his possession.
units.rightText: The slothful man roasteth not that which he took in hunting; But the precious substance of men is to the diligent.

units.leftText: There is life in the path of righteousness, but another path leads to death.
units.rightText: In the way of righteousness is life; And in the pathway thereof there is no death.

units.leftText: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.
units.rightText: A wise son heareth his father’s instruction; But a scoffer heareth not rebuke.

units.leftText: From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.
units.rightText: A man shall eat good by the fruit of his mouth; But the soul of the treacherous shall eat violence.

units.leftText: He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.
units.rightText: He that guardeth his mouth keepeth his life; But he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.

units.leftText: The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.
units.rightText: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing; But the soul of the diligent shall be made fat.

units.leftText: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
units.rightText: A righteous man hateth lying; But a wicked man is loathsome, and cometh to shame.

units.leftText: Righteousness guards the man of integrity, but wickedness undermines the sinner.
units.rightText: Righteousness guardeth him that is upright in the way; But wickedness overthroweth the sinner.

units.leftText: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.
units.rightText: There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: There is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great wealth.

units.leftText: Riches may ransom a man’s life, but a poor man hears no threat.
units.rightText: The ransom of a man’s life is his riches; But the poor heareth no threatening.

units.leftText: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
units.rightText: The light of the righteous rejoiceth; But the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

units.leftText: Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.
units.rightText: By pride cometh only contention; But with the well-advised is wisdom.

units.leftText: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.
units.rightText: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished; But he that gathereth by labor shall have increase.

units.leftText: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
units.rightText: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick; But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.

units.leftText: He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.
units.rightText: Whoso despiseth the word bringeth destruction on himself; But he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded.

units.leftText: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
units.rightText: The law of the wise is a fountain of life, That one may depart from the snares of death.
leftNotes: 13:14 Or law

units.leftText: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.
units.rightText: Good understanding giveth favor; But the way of the transgressor is hard.

units.leftText: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.
units.rightText: Every prudent man worketh with knowledge; But a fool flaunteth his folly.

units.leftText: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
units.rightText: A wicked messenger falleth into evil; But a faithful ambassador is health.

units.leftText: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
units.rightText: Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth correction; But he that regardeth reproof shall be honored.

units.leftText: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.
units.rightText: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul; But it is an abomination to fools to depart from evil.

units.leftText: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
units.rightText: Walk with wise men, and thou shalt be wise; But the companion of fools shall smart for it.

units.leftText: Disaster pursues sinners, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.
units.rightText: Evil pursueth sinners; But the righteous shall be recompensed with good.

units.leftText: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
units.rightText: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children; And the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the righteous.

units.leftText: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.
units.rightText: Much food is in the tillage of the poor; But there is that is destroyed by reason of injustice.

units.leftText: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.
units.rightText: He that spareth his rod hateth his son; But he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.

units.leftText: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.
units.rightText: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his soul; But the belly of the wicked shall want.

units.leftText: Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
units.rightText: Every wise woman buildeth her house; But the foolish plucketh it down with her own hands.

units.leftText: He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but the one who is devious in his ways despises Him.
units.rightText: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth Jehovah; But he that is perverse in his ways despiseth him.

units.leftText: The proud speech of a fool brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
units.rightText: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod for his pride; But the lips of the wise shall preserve them.

units.leftText: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty, but an abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox.
units.rightText: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean; But much increase is by the strength of the ox.

units.leftText: An honest witness does not deceive, but a dishonest witness pours forth lies.
units.rightText: A faithful witness will not lie; But a false witness uttereth lies.

units.leftText: A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
units.rightText: A scoffer seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not; But knowledge is easy unto him that hath understanding.

units.leftText: Stay away from a foolish man; you will gain no knowledge from his speech.
units.rightText: Go into the presence of a foolish man, And thou shalt not perceive in him the lips of knowledge.

units.leftText: The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way, but the folly of fools deceives them.
units.rightText: The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way; But the folly of fools is deceit.

units.leftText: Fools mock the making of amends, but goodwill is found among the upright.
units.rightText: A trespass-offering mocketh fools; But among the upright there is good will.

units.leftText: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy.
units.rightText: The heart knoweth its own bitterness; And a stranger doth not intermeddle with its joy.

units.leftText: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
units.rightText: The house of the wicked shall be overthrown; But the tent of the upright shall flourish.

units.leftText: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
units.rightText: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man; But the end thereof are the ways of death.

units.leftText: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.
units.rightText: Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful; And the end of mirth is heaviness.

units.leftText: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.
units.rightText: The backslider in heart shall be filled with his own ways; And a good man shall be satisfied from himself.

units.leftText: The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.
units.rightText: The simple believeth every word; But the prudent man looketh well to his going.

units.leftText: A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is careless and reckless.
