units.rightText: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil; But the fool beareth himself insolently, and is confident.
leftNotes: 14:16 Or fears the LORD

units.leftText: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.
units.rightText: He that is soon angry will deal foolishly; And a man of wicked devices is hated.

units.leftText: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
units.rightText: The simple inherit folly; But the prudent are crowned with knowledge.

units.leftText: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
units.rightText: The evil bow down before the good; And the wicked, at the gates of the righteous.

units.leftText: The poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but many are those who love the rich.
units.rightText: The poor is hated even of his own neighbor; But the rich hath many friends.

units.leftText: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who shows kindness to the poor.
units.rightText: He that despiseth his neighbor sinneth; But he that hath pity on the poor, happy is he.

units.leftText: Do not those who contrive evil go astray? But those who plan goodness find loving devotion and faithfulness.
units.rightText: Do they not err that devise evil? But mercy and truth shall be to them that devise good.
leftNotes: 14:22 Or show

units.leftText: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
units.rightText: In all labor there is profit; But the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury.

units.leftText: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the effort of fools is folly.
units.rightText: The crown of the wise is their riches; But the folly of fools is only folly.

units.leftText: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who utters lies is deceitful.
units.rightText: A true witness delivereth souls; But he that uttereth lies causeth deceit.

units.leftText: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
units.rightText: In the fear of Jehovah is strong confidence; And his children shall have a place of refuge.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.
units.rightText: The fear of Jehovah is a fountain of life, That one may depart from the snares of death.

units.leftText: A large population is a king’s splendor, but a lack of subjects is a prince’s ruin.
units.rightText: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory; But in the want of people is the destruction of the prince.

units.leftText: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.
units.rightText: He that is slow to anger is of great understanding; But he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.

units.leftText: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
units.rightText: A tranquil heart is the life of the flesh; But envy is the rottenness of the bones.

units.leftText: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
units.rightText: He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker; But he that hath mercy on the needy honoreth him.

units.leftText: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
units.rightText: The wicked is thrust down in his evil-doing; But the righteous hath a refuge in his death.

units.leftText: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning; even among fools she is known.
units.rightText: Wisdom resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding; But that which is in the inward part of fools is made known.
leftNotes: 14:33 Hebrew; LXX and Syriac but among fools she is not known

units.leftText: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
units.rightText: Righteousness exalteth a nation; But sin is a reproach to any people.

units.leftText: A king delights in a wise servant, but his anger falls on the shameful.
units.rightText: The king’s favor is toward a servant that dealeth wisely; But his wrath will be against him that causeth shame.

units.leftText: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
units.rightText: A soft answer turneth away wrath; But a grievous word stirreth up anger.

units.leftText: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.
units.rightText: The tongue of the wise uttereth knowledge aright; But the mouth of fools poureth out folly.

units.leftText: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
units.rightText: The eyes of Jehovah are in every place, Keeping watch upon the evil and the good.

units.leftText: A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.
units.rightText: A gentle tongue is a tree of life; But perverseness therein is a breaking of the spirit.

units.leftText: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
units.rightText: A fool despiseth his father’s correction; But he that regardeth reproof getteth prudence.

units.leftText: The house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble.
units.rightText: In the house of the righteous is much treasure; But in the revenues of the wicked is trouble.

units.leftText: The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but not so the hearts of fools.
units.rightText: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge; But the heart of the foolish doeth not so.

units.leftText: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.
units.rightText: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; But the prayer of the upright is his delight.

units.leftText: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
units.rightText: The way of the wicked is an abomination to Jehovah; But he loveth him that followeth after righteousness.

units.leftText: Discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path; he who hates correction will die.
units.rightText: There is grievous correction for him that forsaketh the way; And he that hateth reproof shall die.

units.leftText: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD— how much more the hearts of men!
units.rightText: Sheol and Abaddon are before Jehovah; How much more then the hearts of the children of men!
leftNotes: 15:11 Or Death and Destruction

units.leftText: A mocker does not love to be reproved, nor will he consult the wise.
units.rightText: A scoffer loveth not to be reproved; He will not go unto the wise.

units.leftText: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.
units.rightText: A glad heart maketh a cheerful countenance; But by sorrow of heart the spirit is broken.

units.leftText: A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
units.rightText: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge; But the mouth of fools feedeth on folly.

units.leftText: All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
units.rightText: All the days of the afflicted are evil; But he that is of a cheerful heart hath a continual feast.

units.leftText: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
units.rightText: Better is little, with the fear of Jehovah, Than great treasure and trouble therewith.

units.leftText: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
units.rightText: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, Than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.

units.leftText: A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger calms dispute.
units.rightText: A wrathful man stirreth up contention; But he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.

units.leftText: The way of the slacker is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.
units.rightText: The way of the sluggard is as a hedge of thorns; But the path of the upright is made a highway.

units.leftText: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.
units.rightText: A wise son maketh a glad father; But a foolish man despiseth his mother.

units.leftText: Folly is joy to one who lacks judgment, but a man of understanding walks a straight path.
units.rightText: Folly is joy to him that is void of wisdom; But a man of understanding maketh straight his going.

units.leftText: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
units.rightText: Where there is no counsel, purposes are disappointed; But in the multitude of counsellors they are established.

units.leftText: A man takes joy in a fitting reply — and how good is a timely word!
units.rightText: A man hath joy in the answer of his mouth; And a word in due season, how good is it!

units.leftText: The path of life leads upward for the wise, that he may avoid going down to Sheol.
units.rightText: To the wise the way of life goeth upward, That he may depart from Sheol beneath.

units.leftText: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He protects the boundaries of the widow.
units.rightText: Jehovah will root up the house of the proud; But he will establish the border of the widow.

units.leftText: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the words of the pure are pleasant to Him.
units.rightText: Evil devices are an abomination to Jehovah; But pleasant words are pure.

units.leftText: He who is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble on his household, but he who hates bribes will live.
units.rightText: He that is greedy of gain troubleth his own house; But he that hateth bribes shall live.

units.leftText: The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.
units.rightText: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer; But the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.

units.leftText: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.
units.rightText: Jehovah is far from the wicked; But he heareth the prayer of the righteous.

units.leftText: The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.
units.rightText: The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart; And good tidings make the bones fat.

units.leftText: He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
units.rightText: The ear that hearkeneth to the reproof of life Shall abide among the wise.

units.leftText: He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.
units.rightText: He that refuseth correction despiseth his own soul; But he that hearkeneth to reproof getteth understanding.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
units.rightText: The fear of Jehovah is the instruction of wisdom; And before honor goeth humility.

units.leftText: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.
units.rightText: The plans of the heart belong to man; But the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah.

units.leftText: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.
units.rightText: All the ways of a man are clean in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the spirits.

units.leftText: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
units.rightText: Commit thy works unto Jehovah, And thy purposes shall be established.

units.leftText: The LORD has made everything for His purpose— even the wicked for the day of disaster.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath made everything for its own end; Yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.

units.leftText: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.
units.rightText: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to Jehovah: Though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.

units.leftText: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.
units.rightText: By mercy and truth iniquity is atoned for; And by the fear of Jehovah men depart from evil.

units.leftText: When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.
units.rightText: When a man’s ways please Jehovah, He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

units.leftText: Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.
units.rightText: Better is a little, with righteousness, Than great revenues with injustice.

units.leftText: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
units.rightText: A man’s heart deviseth his way; But Jehovah directeth his steps.

units.leftText: A divine verdict is on the lips of a king; his mouth must not betray justice.
units.rightText: A divine sentence is in the lips of the king; His mouth shall not transgress in judgment.

units.leftText: Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.
units.rightText: A just balance and scales are Jehovah’s; All the weights of the bag are his work.

units.leftText: Wicked behavior is detestable for kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.
units.rightText: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness; For the throne is established by righteousness.

units.leftText: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, and he who speaks honestly is beloved.
units.rightText: Righteous lips are the delight of kings; And they love him that speaketh right.

units.leftText: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
units.rightText: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death; But a wise man will pacify it.

units.leftText: When a king’s face brightens, there is life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.
units.rightText: In the light of the king’s countenance is life; And his favor is as a cloud of the latter rain.

units.leftText: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is more desirable than silver.
units.rightText: How much better is it to get wisdom than gold! Yea, to get understanding is rather to be chosen than silver.

units.leftText: The highway of the upright leads away from evil; he who guards his way protects his life.
units.rightText: The highway of the upright is to depart from evil: He that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.

units.leftText: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
units.rightText: Pride goeth before destruction, And a haughty spirit before a fall.

units.leftText: It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud.
units.rightText: Better it is to be of a lowly spirit with the poor, Than to divide the spoil with the proud.

units.leftText: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
units.rightText: He that giveth heed unto the word shall find good; And whoso trusteth in Jehovah, happy is he.
leftNotes: 16:20 Or Whoever speaks prudently will find what is good

units.leftText: The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.
units.rightText: The wise in heart shall be called prudent; And the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.

units.leftText: Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.
units.rightText: Understanding is a well-spring of life unto him that hath it; But the correction of fools is their folly.

units.leftText: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.
units.rightText: The heart of the wise instructeth his mouth, And addeth learning to his lips.

units.leftText: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
units.rightText: Pleasant words are as a honeycomb, Sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.

units.leftText: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
units.rightText: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, But the end thereof are the ways of death.

units.leftText: A worker’s appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward.
units.rightText: The appetite of the laboring man laboreth for him; For his mouth urgeth him thereto.

units.leftText: A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.
units.rightText: A worthless man deviseth mischief; And in his lips there is as a scorching fire.
leftNotes: 16:27 Or and what is on his lips

units.leftText: A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.
units.rightText: A perverse man scattereth abroad strife; And a whisperer separateth chief friends.

units.leftText: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.
units.rightText: A man of violence enticeth his neighbor, And leadeth him in a way that is not good.

units.leftText: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.
units.rightText: He that shutteth his eyes, it is to devise perverse things: He that compresseth his lips bringeth evil to pass.

units.leftText: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
units.rightText: The hoary head is a crown of glory; It shall be found in the way of righteousness.

units.leftText: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
units.rightText: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; And he that ruleth his spirit, than he that taketh a city.

units.leftText: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
units.rightText: The lot is cast into the lap; But the whole disposing thereof is of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.
units.rightText: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, Than a house full of feasting with strife.
leftNotes: 17:1 Or sacrifices

units.leftText: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share his inheritance as one of the brothers.
units.rightText: A servant that dealeth wisely shall have rule over a son that causeth shame, And shall have part in the inheritance among the brethren.

units.leftText: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD is the tester of hearts.
units.rightText: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; But Jehovah trieth the hearts.

units.leftText: A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.
units.rightText: An evil-doer giveth heed to wicked lips; And a liar giveth ear to a mischievous tongue.

units.leftText: He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever gloats over calamity will not go unpunished.
units.rightText: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker; And he that is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.

units.leftText: Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of a son is his father.
units.rightText: Children’s children are the crown of old men; And the glory of children are their fathers.

units.leftText: Eloquent words are unfit for a fool; how much worse are lying lips to a ruler!
units.rightText: Excellent speech becometh not a fool; Much less do lying lips a prince.

units.leftText: A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
units.rightText: A bribe is as a precious stone in the eyes of him that hath it; Whithersoever it turneth, it prospereth.

units.leftText: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
units.rightText: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; But he that harpeth on a matter separateth chief friends.

units.leftText: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
units.rightText: A rebuke entereth deeper into one that hath understanding Than a hundred stripes into a fool.

units.leftText: An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
units.rightText: An evil man seeketh only rebellion; Therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

units.leftText: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
units.rightText: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man, Rather than a fool in his folly.

units.leftText: If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
units.rightText: Whoso rewardeth evil for good, Evil shall not depart from his house.

units.leftText: To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
units.rightText: The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: Therefore leave off contention, before there is quarrelling.

units.leftText: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
units.rightText: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the righteous, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.

units.leftText: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
units.rightText: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, Seeing he hath no understanding?

units.leftText: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
units.rightText: A friend loveth at all times; And a brother is born for adversity.

units.leftText: A man lacking judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.
units.rightText: A man void of understanding striketh hands, And becometh surety in the presence of his neighbor.

units.leftText: He who loves transgression loves strife; he who builds his gate high invites destruction.
units.rightText: He loveth transgression that loveth strife: He that raiseth high his gate seeketh destruction.

units.leftText: The one with a perverse heart finds no good, and he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.
units.rightText: He that hath a wayward heart findeth no good; And he that hath a perverse tongue falleth into mischief.

units.leftText: A man fathers a fool to his own grief; the father of a fool has no joy.
units.rightText: He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow; And the father of a fool hath no joy.

units.leftText: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
units.rightText: A cheerful heart is a good medicine; But a broken spirit drieth up the bones.

units.leftText: A wicked man takes a covert bribe to subvert the course of justice.
units.rightText: A wicked man receiveth a bribe out of the bosom, To pervert the ways of justice.
leftNotes: 17:23 Hebrew a bribe from the bosom

units.leftText: Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: Wisdom is before the face of him that hath understanding; But the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.

units.leftText: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him.
units.rightText: A foolish son is a grief to his father, And bitterness to her that bare him.

units.leftText: It is surely not good to punish the innocent or to flog a noble for his honesty.
units.rightText: Also to punish the righteous is not good, Nor to smite the noble for their uprightness.

units.leftText: A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.
units.rightText: He that spareth his words hath knowledge; And he that is of a cool spirit is a man of understanding.

units.leftText: Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.
units.rightText: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise; When he shutteth his lips, he is esteemed as prudent.

units.leftText: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; he rebels against all sound judgment.
units.rightText: He that separateth himself seeketh his own desire, And rageth against all sound wisdom.

units.leftText: A fool does not delight in understanding, but only in airing his opinions.
units.rightText: A fool hath no delight in understanding, But only that his heart may reveal itself.

units.leftText: With a wicked man comes contempt as well, and shame is accompanied by disgrace.
units.rightText: When the wicked cometh, there cometh also contempt, And with ignominy cometh reproach.

units.leftText: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.
units.rightText: The words of a man’s mouth are as deep waters; The wellspring of wisdom is as a flowing brook.

units.leftText: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.
units.rightText: To respect the person of the wicked is not good, Nor to turn aside the righteous in judgment.
leftNotes: 18:5 Hebrew Lifting the face

units.leftText: A fool’s lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.
units.rightText: A fool’s lips enter into contention, And his mouth calleth for stripes.

units.leftText: A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
units.rightText: A fool’s mouth is his destruction, And his lips are the snare of his soul.

units.leftText: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
units.rightText: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.

units.leftText: Whoever is slothful in his work is brother to him who destroys.
units.rightText: He also that is slack in his work Is brother to him that is a destroyer.

units.leftText: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
units.rightText: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower; The righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
leftNotes: 18:10 Or to Him

units.leftText: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.
units.rightText: The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, And as a high wall in his own imagination.

units.leftText: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
units.rightText: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty; And before honor goeth humility.

units.leftText: He who answers a matter before he hears it— this is folly and disgrace to him.
units.rightText: He that giveth answer before he heareth, It is folly and shame unto him.

units.leftText: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?
units.rightText: The spirit of a man will sustain his infirmity; But a broken spirit who can bear?

units.leftText: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.
units.rightText: The heart of the prudent getteth knowledge; And the ear of the wise seeketh knowledge.

units.leftText: A man’s gift opens doors for him, and brings him before great men.
units.rightText: A man’s gift maketh room for him, And bringeth him before great men.

units.leftText: The first to state his case seems right until another comes and cross-examines him.
units.rightText: He that pleadeth his cause first seemeth just; But his neighbor cometh and searcheth him out.

units.leftText: Casting the lot ends quarrels and separates strong opponents.
units.rightText: The lot causeth contentions to cease, And parteth between the mighty.

units.leftText: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
units.rightText: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city; And such contentions are like the bars of a castle.

units.leftText: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.
units.rightText: A man’s belly shall be filled with the fruit of his mouth; With the increase of his lips shall he be satisfied.

units.leftText: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
units.rightText: Death and life are in the power of the tongue; And they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

units.leftText: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
units.rightText: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, And obtaineth favor of Jehovah.

units.leftText: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.
units.rightText: The poor useth entreaties; But the rich answereth roughly.

units.leftText: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
units.rightText: He that maketh many friends doeth it to his own destruction; But there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.

units.leftText: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
units.rightText: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity Than he that is perverse in his lips and is a fool.

units.leftText: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
units.rightText: Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good; And he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.

units.leftText: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
units.rightText: The foolishness of man subverteth his way; And his heart fretteth against Jehovah.

units.leftText: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.
units.rightText: Wealth addeth many friends; But the poor is separated from his friend.

units.leftText: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.
units.rightText: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall not escape.

units.leftText: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
units.rightText: Many will entreat the favor of the liberal man; And every man is a friend to him that giveth gifts.

units.leftText: All the brothers of a poor man hate him — how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
units.rightText: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: How much more do his friends go far from him! He pursueth them with words, but they are gone.

units.leftText: He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find success.
units.rightText: He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: He that keepeth understanding shall find good.

units.leftText: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.
units.rightText: A false witness shall not be unpunished; And he that uttereth lies shall perish.

units.leftText: Luxury is unseemly for a fool— how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
units.rightText: Delicate living is not seemly for a fool; Much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

units.leftText: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
units.rightText: The discretion of a man maketh him slow to anger; And it is his glory to pass over a transgression.

units.leftText: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
units.rightText: The king’s wrath is as the roaring of a lion; But his favor is as dew upon the grass.

units.leftText: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.
units.rightText: A foolish son is the calamity of his father; And the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping.

units.leftText: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
units.rightText: House and riches are an inheritance from fathers; But a prudent wife is from Jehovah.

units.leftText: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
units.rightText: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; And the idle soul shall suffer hunger.

units.leftText: He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.
units.rightText: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul; But he that is careless of his ways shall die.

units.leftText: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
units.rightText: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Jehovah, And his good deed will he pay him again.

units.leftText: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
units.rightText: Chasten thy son, seeing there is hope; And set not thy heart on his destruction.

units.leftText: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.
units.rightText: A man of great wrath shall bear the penalty; For if thou deliver him, thou must do it yet again.

units.leftText: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
units.rightText: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, That thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.

units.leftText: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
units.rightText: There are many devices in a man’s heart; But the counsel of Jehovah, that shall stand.

units.leftText: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.
units.rightText: That which maketh a man to be desired is his kindness; And a poor man is better than a liar.

units.leftText: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.
units.rightText: The fear of Jehovah tendeth to life; And he that hath it shall abide satisfied; He shall not be visited with evil.

units.leftText: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.
units.rightText: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish, And will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.

units.leftText: Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.
units.rightText: Smite a scoffer, and the simple will learn prudence; And reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge.

units.leftText: He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
units.rightText: He that doeth violence to his father, and chaseth away his mother, Is a son that causeth shame and bringeth reproach.

units.leftText: If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.
units.rightText: Cease, my son, to hear instruction Only to err from the words of knowledge.

units.leftText: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and a wicked mouth swallows iniquity.
units.rightText: A worthless witness mocketh at justice; And the mouth of the wicked swalloweth iniquity.

units.leftText: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
units.rightText: Judgments are prepared for scoffers, And stripes for the back of fools.

units.leftText: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
units.rightText: Wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler; And whosoever erreth thereby is not wise.

units.leftText: The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his own life.
units.rightText: The terror of a king is as the roaring of a lion: He that provoketh him to anger sinneth against his own life.
leftNotes: 20:2 Literally sins against his own soul

units.leftText: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.
units.rightText: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife; But every fool will be quarrelling.

units.leftText: The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.
units.rightText: The sluggard will not plow by reason of the winter; Therefore he shall beg in harvest, and have nothing.

units.leftText: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.
units.rightText: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water; But a man of understanding will draw it out.

units.leftText: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?
units.rightText: Most men will proclaim every one his own kindness; But a faithful man who can find?

units.leftText: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.
units.rightText: A righteous man that walketh in his integrity, Blessed are his children after him.

units.leftText: A king who sits on a throne to judge sifts out all evil with his eyes.
units.rightText: A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment Scattereth away all evil with his eyes.

units.leftText: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?
units.rightText: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?

units.leftText: Differing weights and unequal measures — both are detestable to the LORD.
units.rightText: Diverse weights, and diverse measures, Both of them alike are an abomination to Jehovah.
leftNotes: 20:10 Hebrew A stone and a stone, an ephah and an ephah

units.leftText: Even a young man is known by his actions— whether his conduct is pure and upright.
units.rightText: Even a child maketh himself known by his doings, Whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.

units.leftText: Ears that hear and eyes that see— the LORD has made them both.
units.rightText: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, Jehovah hath made even both of them.

units.leftText: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.
units.rightText: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; Open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.

units.leftText: “Worthless, worthless!” says the buyer, but on the way out, he gloats.
units.rightText: It is bad, it is bad, saith the buyer; But when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.

units.leftText: There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but lips of knowledge are a rare treasure.
units.rightText: There is gold, and abundance of rubies; But the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.

units.leftText: Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
units.rightText: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge that is surety for foreigners.
leftNotes: 20:16 Or a wayward woman

units.leftText: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel.
units.rightText: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man; But afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

units.leftText: Set plans by consultation, and wage war under sound guidance.
units.rightText: Every purpose is established by counsel; And by wise guidance make thou war.

units.leftText: He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.
units.rightText: He that goeth about as a tale-bearer revealeth secrets; Therefore company not with him that openeth wide his lips.
leftNotes: 20:19 Or the one who is simple

units.leftText: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.
units.rightText: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, His lamp shall be put out in blackness of darkness.

units.leftText: An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.
units.rightText: An inheritance may be gotten hastily at the beginning; But the end thereof shall not be blessed.

units.leftText: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
units.rightText: Say not thou, I will recompense evil: Wait for Jehovah, and he will save thee.

units.leftText: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good.
units.rightText: Diverse weights are an abomination to Jehovah; And a false balance is not good.

units.leftText: A man’s steps are from the LORD, so how can anyone understand his own way?
units.rightText: A man’s goings are of Jehovah; How then can man understand his way?

units.leftText: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.
units.rightText: It is a snare to a man rashly to say, It is holy, And after vows to make inquiry.

units.leftText: A wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
units.rightText: A wise king winnoweth the wicked, And bringeth the threshing-wheel over them.

units.leftText: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being.
units.rightText: The spirit of man is the lamp of Jehovah, Searching all his innermost parts.
leftNotes: 20:27 Or breath or speech

units.leftText: Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king; by these he maintains his throne.
units.rightText: Kindness and truth preserve the king; And his throne is upholden by kindness.

units.leftText: The glory of young men is their strength, and gray hair is the splendor of the old.
units.rightText: The glory of young men is their strength; And the beauty of old men is the hoary head.

units.leftText: Lashes and wounds scour evil, and beatings cleanse the inmost parts.
units.rightText: Stripes that wound cleanse away evil; And strokes reach the innermost parts.

units.leftText: The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.
units.rightText: The king’s heart is in the hand of Jehovah as the watercourses: He turneth it whithersoever he will.

units.leftText: All a man’s ways seem right to him, but the LORD weighs the heart.
units.rightText: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes; But Jehovah weigheth the hearts.

units.leftText: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice.
units.rightText: To do righteousness and justice Is more acceptable to Jehovah than sacrifice.

units.leftText: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— the guides of the wicked— are sin.
units.rightText: A high look, and a proud heart, Even the lamp of the wicked, is sin.

units.leftText: The plans of the diligent bring plenty, as surely as haste leads to poverty.
units.rightText: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; But every one that is hasty hasteth only to want.

units.leftText: Making a fortune by a lying tongue is a vanishing mist, a deadly pursuit.
units.rightText: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue Is a vapor driven to and fro by them that seek death.

units.leftText: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away because they refuse to do what is just.
units.rightText: The violence of the wicked shall sweep them away, Because they refuse to do justice.

units.leftText: The way of a guilty man is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
units.rightText: The way of him that is laden with guilt is exceeding crooked; But as for the pure, his work is right.

units.leftText: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
units.rightText: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.

units.leftText: The soul of the wicked man craves evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.
units.rightText: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: His neighbor findeth no favor in his eyes.

units.leftText: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; and when a wise man is instructed, he acquires knowledge.
units.rightText: When the scoffer is punished, the simple is made wise; And when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.

units.leftText: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.
units.rightText: The righteous man considereth the house of the wicked, How the wicked are overthrown to their ruin.
leftNotes: 21:12 Or The righteous one

units.leftText: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, he too shall cry out and receive no answer.
units.rightText: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, He also shall cry, but shall not be heard.

units.leftText: A gift in secret soothes anger, and a covert bribe pacifies great wrath.
units.rightText: A gift in secret pacifieth anger; And a present in the bosom, strong wrath.
leftNotes: 21:14 Hebrew a bribe in the bosom

units.leftText: Justice executed is a joy to the righteous, but a terror to the workers of iniquity.
units.rightText: It is joy to the righteous to do justice; But it is a destruction to the workers of iniquity.

units.leftText: The man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.
units.rightText: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding Shall rest in the assembly of the dead.

units.leftText: He who loves pleasure will become poor; the one who loves wine and oil will never be rich.
units.rightText: He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: He that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.

units.leftText: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless for the upright.
units.rightText: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous; And the treacherous cometh in the stead of the upright.

units.leftText: Better to live in the desert than with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.
units.rightText: It is better to dwell in a desert land, Than with a contentious and fretful woman.

units.leftText: Precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man consumes them.
units.rightText: There is precious treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise; But a foolish man swalloweth it up.

units.leftText: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.
units.rightText: He that followeth after righteousness and kindness Findeth life, righteousness, and honor.

units.leftText: A wise man scales the city of the mighty and pulls down the stronghold in which they trust.
units.rightText: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty, And bringeth down the strength of the confidence thereof.

units.leftText: He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress.
units.rightText: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue Keepeth his soul from troubles.

units.leftText: Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man — of him who acts with excessive pride.
units.rightText: The proud and haughty man, scoffer is his name; He worketh in the arrogance of pride.

units.leftText: The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.
units.rightText: The desire of the sluggard killeth him; For his hands refuse to labor.

units.leftText: All day long he covets more, but the righteous give without restraint.
units.rightText: There is that coveteth greedily all the day long; But the righteous giveth and withholdeth not.

units.leftText: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable— how much more so when brought with ill intent!
units.rightText: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; How much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind!

units.leftText: A lying witness will perish, but the man who listens to truth will speak forever.
units.rightText: A false witness shall perish; But the man that heareth shall speak so as to endure.

units.leftText: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright man makes his way sure.
units.rightText: A wicked man hardeneth his face; But as for the upright, he establisheth his ways.
leftNotes: 21:29 Or puts up a bold front

units.leftText: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD.
units.rightText: There is no wisdom nor understanding Nor counsel against Jehovah.

units.leftText: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
units.rightText: The horse is prepared against the day of battle; But victory is of Jehovah.

units.leftText: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.
units.rightText: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, And loving favor rather than silver and gold.

units.leftText: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.
units.rightText: The rich and the poor meet together: Jehovah is the maker of them all.

units.leftText: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.
units.rightText: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

units.leftText: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.
units.rightText: The reward of humility and the fear of Jehovah Is riches, and honor, and life.

units.leftText: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; he who guards his soul stays far from them.
units.rightText: Thorns and snares are in the way of the perverse: He that keepeth his soul shall be far from them.

units.leftText: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
units.rightText: Train up a child in the way he should go, And even when he is old he will not depart from it.

units.leftText: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
units.rightText: The rich ruleth over the poor; And the borrower is servant to the lender.

units.leftText: He who sows injustice will reap disaster, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
units.rightText: He that soweth iniquity shall reap calamity; And the rod of his wrath shall fail.
leftNotes: 22:8 LXX includes God blesses a cheerful and generous man, but foolish works will come to an end; see also 2 Corinthians 9:7|2CO 9:7*.

units.leftText: A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.
units.rightText: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; For he giveth of his bread to the poor.
leftNotes: 22:9 Literally He whose eye is good

units.leftText: Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart; even quarreling and insults will cease.
units.rightText: Cast out the scoffer, and contention will go out; Yea, strife and ignominy will cease.

units.leftText: He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.
units.rightText: He that loveth pureness of heart, For the grace of his lips the king will be his friend.

units.leftText: The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge, but He frustrates the words of the faithless.
units.rightText: The eyes of Jehovah preserve him that hath knowledge; But he overthroweth the words of the treacherous man.

units.leftText: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!”
units.rightText: The sluggard saith, There is a lion without; I shall be slain in the streets.

units.leftText: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; he who is under the wrath of the LORD will fall into it.
units.rightText: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit; He that is abhorred of Jehovah shall fall therein.

units.leftText: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
units.rightText: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child; But the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

units.leftText: Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty. Thirty Sayings of the Wise Saying 1
units.rightText: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his gain, And he that giveth to the rich, shall come only to want.

units.leftText: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise — apply your mind to my knowledge —
units.rightText: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, And apply thy heart unto my knowledge.

units.leftText: for it is pleasing when you keep them within you and they are constantly on your lips.
units.rightText: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee, If they be established together upon thy lips.

units.leftText: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I instruct you today — yes, you.
units.rightText: That thy trust may be in Jehovah, I have made them known to thee this day, even to thee.

units.leftText: Have I not written for you thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge,
units.rightText: Have not I written unto thee excellent things Of counsels and knowledge,
leftNotes: 22:20 Or written for you excellent sayings or written for you three times

units.leftText: to show you true and reliable words, that you may soundly answer those who sent you? Saying 2
units.rightText: To make thee know the certainty of the words of truth, That thou mayest carry back words of truth to them that send thee?

units.leftText: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,
units.rightText: Rob not the poor, because he is poor; Neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:

units.leftText: for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who rob them. Saying 3
units.rightText: For Jehovah will plead their cause, And despoil of life those that despoil them.

units.leftText: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,
units.rightText: Make no friendship with a man that is given to anger; And with a wrathful man thou shalt not go:

units.leftText: or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare. Saying 4
units.rightText: Lest thou learn his ways, And get a snare to thy soul.

units.leftText: Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.
units.rightText: Be thou not one of them that strike hands, Or of them that are sureties for debts.

units.leftText: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you? Saying 5
units.rightText: If thou hast not wherewith to pay, Why should he take away thy bed from under thee?

units.leftText: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed. Saying 6
units.rightText: Remove not the ancient landmark, Which thy fathers have set.

units.leftText: Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will be stationed in the presence of kings; he will not stand before obscure men.
units.rightText: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; He shall not stand before mean men.

units.leftText: When you sit down to dine with a ruler, consider carefully what is set before you,
units.rightText: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, Consider diligently him that is before thee;
leftNotes: 23:1 Or who is before you

units.leftText: and put a knife to your throat if you possess a great appetite.
units.rightText: And put a knife to thy throat, If thou be a man given to appetite.

units.leftText: Do not crave his delicacies, for that food is deceptive. Saying 8
units.rightText: Be not desirous of his dainties; Seeing they are deceitful food.

units.leftText: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; be wise enough to restrain yourself.
units.rightText: Weary not thyself to be rich; Cease from thine own wisdom.

units.leftText: When you glance at wealth, it disappears, for it makes wings for itself and flies like an eagle to the sky. Saying 9
units.rightText: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? For riches certainly make themselves wings, Like an eagle that flieth toward heaven.

units.leftText: Do not eat the bread of a stingy man, and do not crave his delicacies;
units.rightText: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, Neither desire thou his dainties:
leftNotes: 23:6 Literally of him whose eye is evil

units.leftText: for he is keeping track, inwardly counting the cost. “Eat and drink,” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
units.rightText: For as he thinketh within himself, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; But his heart is not with thee.
leftNotes: 23:7 Or for as he calculates in his soul, so is he

units.leftText: You will vomit up what little you have eaten and waste your pleasant words. Saying 10
units.rightText: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, And lose thy sweet words.

units.leftText: Do not speak to a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words. Saying 11
units.rightText: Speak not in the hearing of a fool; For he will despise the wisdom of thy words.

units.leftText: Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
units.rightText: Remove not the ancient landmark; And enter not into the fields of the fatherless:

units.leftText: for their Redeemer is strong; He will take up their case against you. Saying 12
units.rightText: For their Redeemer is strong; He will plead their cause against thee.

units.leftText: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge. Saying 13
units.rightText: Apply thy heart unto instruction, And thine ears to the words of knowledge.

units.leftText: Do not withhold discipline from a child; although you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
units.rightText: Withhold not correction from the child; For if thou beat him with the rod, he will not die.

units.leftText: Strike him with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol. Saying 14
units.rightText: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, And shalt deliver his soul from Sheol.

units.leftText: My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will indeed rejoice.
units.rightText: My son, if thy heart be wise, My heart will be glad, even mine:

units.leftText: My inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right. Saying 15
units.rightText: Yea, my heart will rejoice, When thy lips speak right things.
leftNotes: 23:16 Hebrew My kidneys

units.leftText: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD.
units.rightText: Let not thy heart envy sinners; But be thou in the fear of Jehovah all the day long:

units.leftText: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off. Saying 16
units.rightText: For surely there is a reward; And thy hope shall not be cut off.

units.leftText: Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right course.
units.rightText: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And guide thy heart in the way.

units.leftText: Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat.
units.rightText: Be not among winebibbers, Among gluttonous eaters of flesh:

units.leftText: For the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe them in rags. Saying 17
units.rightText: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty; And drowsiness will clothe a man with rags.

units.leftText: Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
units.rightText: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, And despise not thy mother when she is old.

units.leftText: Invest in truth and never sell it— in wisdom and instruction and understanding.
units.rightText: Buy the truth, and sell it not; Yea, wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.

units.leftText: The father of a righteous man will greatly rejoice, and he who fathers a wise son will delight in him.
units.rightText: The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice; And he that begetteth a wise child will have joy of him.

units.leftText: May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice! Saying 18
units.rightText: Let thy father and thy mother be glad, And let her that bare thee rejoice.

units.leftText: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.
units.rightText: My son, give me thy heart; And let thine eyes delight in my ways.

units.leftText: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and an adulteress is a narrow well.
units.rightText: For a harlot is a deep ditch; And a foreign woman is a narrow pit.
leftNotes: 23:27 Or a foreign woman or a wayward wife

units.leftText: Like a robber she lies in wait and multiplies the faithless among men. Saying 19
units.rightText: Yea, she lieth in wait as a robber, And increaseth the treacherous among men.

units.leftText: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who has needless wounds? Who has bloodshot eyes?
units.rightText: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? Who hath complaining? who hath wounds without cause? Who hath redness of eyes?

units.leftText: Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed drinks.
units.rightText: They that tarry long at the wine; They that go to seek out mixed wine.

units.leftText: Do not gaze at wine while it is red, when it sparkles in the cup and goes down smoothly.
units.rightText: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, When it sparkleth in the cup, When it goeth down smoothly:

units.leftText: In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
units.rightText: At the last it biteth like a serpent, And stingeth like an adder.

units.leftText: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will utter perversities.
units.rightText: Thine eyes shall behold strange things, And thy heart shall utter perverse things.

units.leftText: You will be like one sleeping on the high seas or lying on the top of a mast:
units.rightText: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, Or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.

units.leftText: “They struck me, but I feel no pain! They beat me, but I did not know it! When can I wake up to search for another drink?”
units.rightText: They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not hurt; They have beaten me, and I felt it not: When shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.

units.leftText: Do not envy wicked men or desire their company;
units.rightText: Be not thou envious against evil men; Neither desire to be with them:

units.leftText: for their hearts devise violence, and their lips declare trouble. Saying 21
units.rightText: For their heart studieth oppression, And their lips talk of mischief.

units.leftText: By wisdom a house is built and by understanding it is established;
units.rightText: Through wisdom is a house builded; And by understanding it is established;

units.leftText: through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure. Saying 22
units.rightText: And by knowledge are the chambers filled With all precious and pleasant riches.

units.leftText: A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge enhances his strength.
units.rightText: A wise man is strong; Yea, a man of knowledge increaseth might.
leftNotes: 24:5 LXX The wise are mightier than the strong

units.leftText: Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors. Saying 23
units.rightText: For by wise guidance thou shalt make thy war; And in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

units.leftText: Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place. Saying 24
units.rightText: Wisdom is too high for a fool: He openeth not his mouth in the gate.

units.leftText: He who plots evil will be called a schemer.
units.rightText: He that deviseth to do evil, Men shall call him a mischief-maker.

units.leftText: A foolish scheme is sin, and a mocker is detestable to men. Saying 25
units.rightText: The thought of foolishness is sin; And the scoffer is an abomination to men.

units.leftText: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!
units.rightText: If thou faint in the day of adversity, Thy strength is small.

units.leftText: Rescue those being led away to death, and restrain those stumbling toward the slaughter.
units.rightText: Deliver them that are carried away unto death, And those that are ready to be slain see that thou hold back.

units.leftText: If you say, “Behold, we did not know about this,” does not He who weighs hearts consider it? Does not the One who guards your life know? Will He not repay a man according to his deeds? Saying 26
units.rightText: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew not this; Doth not he that weigheth the hearts consider it? And he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? And shall not he render to every man according to his work?

units.leftText: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
units.rightText: My son, eat thou honey, for it is good; And the droppings of the honeycomb, which are sweet to thy taste:

units.leftText: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off. Saying 27
units.rightText: So shalt thou know wisdom to be unto thy soul; If thou hast found it, then shall there be a reward, And thy hope shall not be cut off.

units.leftText: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy his resting place.
units.rightText: Lay not wait, O wicked man, against the habitation of the righteous; Destroy not his resting-place:

units.leftText: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times. Saying 28
units.rightText: For a righteous man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; But the wicked are overthrown by calamity.

units.leftText: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,
units.rightText: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, And let not thy heart be glad when he is overthrown;

units.leftText: or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him. Saying 29
units.rightText: Lest Jehovah see it, and it displease him, And he turn away his wrath from him.

units.leftText: Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.
units.rightText: Fret not thyself because of evil-doers; Neither be thou envious at the wicked:

units.leftText: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished. Saying 30
units.rightText: For there shall be no reward to the evil man; The lamp of the wicked shall be put out.

units.leftText: My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.
units.rightText: My son, fear thou Jehovah and the king; And company not with them that are given to change:

units.leftText: For they will bring sudden destruction. Who knows what ruin they can bring? Further Sayings of the Wise
units.rightText: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; And the destruction from them both, who knoweth it?

units.leftText: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
units.rightText: These also are sayings of the wise. To have respect of persons in judgment is not good.

units.leftText: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”— peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him;
units.rightText: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous, Peoples shall curse him, nations shall abhor him;

units.leftText: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come upon them.
units.rightText: But to them that rebuke him shall be delight, And a good blessing shall come upon them.

units.leftText: An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips.
units.rightText: He kisseth the lips Who giveth a right answer.

units.leftText: Complete your outdoor work and prepare your field; after that, you may build your house.
units.rightText: Prepare thy work without, And make it ready for thee in the field; And afterwards build thy house.

units.leftText: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.
units.rightText: Be not a witness against thy neighbor without cause; And deceive not with thy lips.

units.leftText: Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
units.rightText: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me; I will render to the man according to his work.

units.leftText: I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
units.rightText: I went by the field of the sluggard, And by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;

units.leftText: Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.
units.rightText: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, The face thereof was covered with nettles, And the stone wall thereof was broken down.

units.leftText: I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction:
units.rightText: Then I beheld, and considered well; I saw, and received instruction:

units.leftText: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
units.rightText: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to sleep;

units.leftText: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
units.rightText: So shall thy poverty come as a robber, And thy want as an armed man.

units.leftText: These are additional proverbs of Solomon, which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:
units.rightText: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

units.leftText: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out.
units.rightText: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.

units.leftText: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings cannot be searched.
units.rightText: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.

units.leftText: Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth.
units.rightText: Take away the dross from the silver, And there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner:

units.leftText: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
units.rightText: Take away the wicked from before the king, And his throne shall be established in righteousness.

units.leftText: Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of great men;
units.rightText: Put not thyself forward in the presence of the king, And stand not in the place of great men:

units.leftText: for it is better to be told, “Come up here!” than to be demoted in the presence of the prince. Even what you have seen with your own eyes,
units.rightText: For better is it that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, Than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince, Whom thine eyes have seen.
leftNotes: 25:7 Or Even the one

units.leftText: do not bring hastily to court. Otherwise, what will you do in the end when your neighbor puts you to shame?
units.rightText: Go not forth hastily to strive, Lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, When thy neighbor hath put thee to shame.

units.leftText: Argue your case with your neighbor without betraying another’s confidence,
units.rightText: Debate thy cause with thy neighbor himself, And disclose not the secret of another;

units.leftText: lest he who hears you bring shame upon you, and your infamy never go away.
units.rightText: Lest he that heareth it revile thee, And thine infamy turn not away.

units.leftText: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
units.rightText: A word fitly spoken Is like apples of gold in network of silver.

units.leftText: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.
units.rightText: As an ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, So is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

units.leftText: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters.
units.rightText: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, So is a faithful messenger to them that send him; For he refresheth the soul of his masters.

units.leftText: Like clouds and wind without rain is the man who boasts of gifts never given.
units.rightText: As clouds and wind without rain, So is he that boasteth himself of his gifts falsely.

units.leftText: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
units.rightText: By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

units.leftText: If you find honey, eat just what you need, lest you have too much and vomit it up.
units.rightText: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, Lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

units.leftText: Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house, lest he grow weary and hate you.
units.rightText: Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbor’s house, Lest he be weary of thee, and hate thee.

units.leftText: Like a club or sword or sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbor.
units.rightText: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbor Is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

units.leftText: Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble.
units.rightText: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble Is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

units.leftText: Like one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
units.rightText: As one that taketh off a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon soda, So is he that singeth songs to a heavy heart.
leftNotes: 25:20 Or on soda

units.leftText: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
units.rightText: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

units.leftText: For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
units.rightText: For thou wilt heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward thee.
leftNotes: 25:22 LXX; Hebrew For you will heap burning coals on his head; cited in Romans 12:20|ROM 12:20*

units.leftText: As the north wind brings forth rain, so a backbiting tongue brings angry looks.
units.rightText: The north wind bringeth forth rain; So doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance.

units.leftText: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
units.rightText: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.

units.leftText: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
units.rightText: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.

units.leftText: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.
units.rightText: As a troubled fountain, and a corrupted spring, So is a righteous man that giveth way before the wicked.

units.leftText: It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory.
units.rightText: It is not good to eat much honey; So for men to search out their own glory is grievous.

units.leftText: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper.
units.rightText: He whose spirit is without restraint Is like a city that is broken down and without walls.

units.leftText: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor does not befit a fool.
units.rightText: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, So honor is not seemly for a fool.

units.leftText: Like a fluttering sparrow or darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.
units.rightText: As the sparrow in her wandering, as the swallow in her flying, So the curse that is causeless alighteth not.

units.leftText: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!
units.rightText: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, And a rod for the back of fools.

units.leftText: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will be like him.
units.rightText: Answer not a fool according to his folly, Lest thou also be like unto him.

units.leftText: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.
units.rightText: Answer a fool according to his folly, Lest he be wise in his own conceit.

units.leftText: Like cutting off one’s own feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.
units.rightText: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool Cutteth off his own feet, and drinketh in damage.

units.leftText: Like lame legs hanging limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
units.rightText: The legs of the lame hang loose; So is a parable in the mouth of fools.

units.leftText: Like binding a stone into a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.
units.rightText: As one that bindeth a stone in a sling, So is he that giveth honor to a fool.

units.leftText: Like a thorn that goes into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
units.rightText: As a thorn that goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, So is a parable in the mouth of fools.

units.leftText: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or passerby.
units.rightText: As an archer that woundeth all, So is he that hireth a fool and he that hireth them that pass by.

units.leftText: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
units.rightText: As a dog that returneth to his vomit, So is a fool that repeateth his folly.
leftNotes: 26:11 Cited in 2 Peter 2:22|2PE 2:22*

units.leftText: Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
units.rightText: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope of a fool than of him.

units.leftText: The slacker says, “A lion is in the road! A fierce lion roams the public square!”
units.rightText: The sluggard saith, There is a lion in the way; A lion is in the streets.

units.leftText: As a door turns on its hinges, so the slacker turns on his bed.
units.rightText: As the door turneth upon its hinges, So doth the sluggard upon his bed.

units.leftText: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; it wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.
units.rightText: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish; It wearieth him to bring it again to his mouth.

units.leftText: The slacker is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.
units.rightText: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit Than seven men that can render a reason.

units.leftText: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
units.rightText: He that passeth by, and vexeth himself with strife belonging not to him, Is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.

units.leftText: Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows,
units.rightText: As a madman who casteth firebrands, Arrows, and death,

units.leftText: so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
units.rightText: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbor, And saith, Am not I in sport?

units.leftText: Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.
units.rightText: For lack of wood the fire goeth out; And where there is no whisperer, contention ceaseth.

units.leftText: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
units.rightText: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, So is a contentious man to inflame strife.

units.leftText: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
units.rightText: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, And they go down into the innermost parts.

units.leftText: Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are burning lips and a wicked heart.
units.rightText: Fervent lips and a wicked heart Are like an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross.
leftNotes: 26:23 Hebrew; LXX smooth

units.leftText: A hateful man disguises himself with his speech, but he lays up deceit in his heart.
units.rightText: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips; But he layeth up deceit within him:

units.leftText: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.
units.rightText: When he speaketh fair, believe him not; For there are seven abominations in his heart:

units.leftText: Though his hatred is concealed by deception, his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
units.rightText: Though his hatred cover itself with guile, His wickedness shall be openly showed before the assembly.

units.leftText: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.
