units.rightText: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein; And he that rolleth a stone, it shall return upon him.

units.leftText: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.
units.rightText: A lying tongue hateth those whom it hath wounded; And a flattering mouth worketh ruin.

units.leftText: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
units.rightText: Boast not thyself of to-morrow; For thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

units.leftText: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth— a stranger, and not your own lips.
units.rightText: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; A stranger, and not thine own lips.

units.leftText: A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but aggravation from a fool outweighs them both.
units.rightText: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; But a fool’s vexation is heavier than they both.

units.leftText: Wrath is cruel and anger is like a flood, but who can withstand jealousy?
units.rightText: Wrath is cruel, and anger is overwhelming; But who is able to stand before jealousy?

units.leftText: Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed.
units.rightText: Better is open rebuke Than love that is hidden.

units.leftText: The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
units.rightText: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; But the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

units.leftText: The soul that is full loathes honey, but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.
units.rightText: The full soul loatheth a honeycomb; But to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

units.leftText: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who wanders from his home.
units.rightText: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, So is a man that wandereth from his place.

units.leftText: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the counsel of a friend is sweetness to the soul.
units.rightText: Oil and perfume rejoice the heart; So doth the sweetness of a man’s friend that cometh of hearty counsel.

units.leftText: Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend, and do not go to your brother’s house in the day of your calamity; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
units.rightText: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; And go not to thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother far off.

units.leftText: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me.
units.rightText: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, That I may answer him that reproacheth me.

units.leftText: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
units.rightText: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself; But the simple pass on, and suffer for it.

units.leftText: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
units.rightText: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger; And hold him in pledge that is surety for a foreign woman.
leftNotes: 27:13 Or a wayward woman

units.leftText: If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.
units.rightText: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, It shall be counted a curse to him.

units.leftText: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike —
units.rightText: A continual dropping in a very rainy day And a contentious woman are alike:

units.leftText: restraining her is like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.
units.rightText: He that would restrain her restraineth the wind; And his right hand encountereth oil.

units.leftText: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
units.rightText: Iron sharpeneth iron; So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
leftNotes: 27:17 Hebrew sharpens the face of another or sharpens the countenance of a friend

units.leftText: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.
units.rightText: Whoso keepeth the fig-tree shall eat the fruit thereof; And he that regardeth his master shall be honored.

units.leftText: As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the true man.
units.rightText: As in water face answereth to face, So the heart of man to man.

units.leftText: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
units.rightText: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; And the eyes of man are never satisfied.
leftNotes: 27:20 Or Death and Destruction

units.leftText: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is tested by the praise accorded him.
units.rightText: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold; And a man is tried by his praise.

units.leftText: Though you grind a fool like grain with mortar and a pestle, yet his folly will not depart from him.
units.rightText: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle along with bruised grain, Yet will not his foolishness depart from him.

units.leftText: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds;
units.rightText: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, And look well to thy herds:

units.leftText: for riches are not forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.
units.rightText: For riches are not for ever; And doth the crown endure unto all generations?

units.leftText: When hay is removed and new growth appears and the grass from the hills is gathered,
units.rightText: The hay is carried, and the tender grass showeth itself, And the herbs of the mountains are gathered in.

units.leftText: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.
units.rightText: The lambs are for thy clothing, And the goats are the price of the field;

units.leftText: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you— food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants.
units.rightText: And there will be goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, And maintenance for thy maidens.

units.leftText: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
units.rightText: The wicked flee when no man pursueth; But the righteous are bold as a lion.

units.leftText: A land in rebellion has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.
units.rightText: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof; But by men of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.

units.leftText: A destitute leader who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
units.rightText: A needy man that oppresseth the poor Is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.

units.leftText: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.
units.rightText: They that forsake the law praise the wicked; But such as keep the law contend with them.

units.leftText: Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD comprehend fully.
units.rightText: Evil men understand not justice; But they that seek Jehovah understand all things.

units.leftText: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.
units.rightText: Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, Than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.

units.leftText: A discerning son keeps the law, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.
units.rightText: Whoso keepeth the law is a wise son; But he that is a companion of gluttons shameth his father.

units.leftText: He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
units.rightText: He that augmenteth his substance by interest and increase, Gathereth it for him that hath pity on the poor.

units.leftText: Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.
units.rightText: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, Even his prayer is an abomination.

units.leftText: He who leads the upright along the path of evil will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit what is good.
units.rightText: Whoso causeth the upright to go astray in an evil way, He shall fall himself into his own pit; But the perfect shall inherit good.

units.leftText: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.
units.rightText: The rich man is wise in his own conceit; But the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.

units.leftText: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
units.rightText: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory; But when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.

units.leftText: He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.
units.rightText: He that covereth his transgressions shall not prosper; But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall obtain mercy.

units.leftText: Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but he who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
units.rightText: Happy is the man that feareth alway; But he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
leftNotes: 28:14 Or always fears the LORD; Hebrew does not include the LORD.

units.leftText: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
units.rightText: As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear, So is a wicked ruler over a poor people.

units.leftText: A leader who lacks judgment is also a great oppressor, but he who hates dishonest profit will prolong his days.
units.rightText: The prince that lacketh understanding is also a great oppressor; But he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.

units.leftText: A man burdened by bloodguilt will flee into the Pit; let no one support him.
units.rightText: A man that is laden with the blood of any person Shall flee unto the pit; let no man stay him.
leftNotes: 28:17 Or will be a fugitive until death

units.leftText: He who walks with integrity will be kept safe, but whoever is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall.
units.rightText: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be delivered; But he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once.

units.leftText: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
units.rightText: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread; But he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough.

units.leftText: A faithful man will abound with blessings, but one eager to be rich will not go unpunished.
units.rightText: A faithful man shall abound with blessings; But he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be unpunished.

units.leftText: To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
units.rightText: To have respect of persons is not good; Neither that a man should transgress for a piece of bread.

units.leftText: A stingy man hastens after wealth and does not know that poverty awaits him.
units.rightText: He that hath an evil eye hasteth after riches, And knoweth not that want shall come upon him.
leftNotes: 28:22 Hebrew A man whose eye is evil

units.leftText: He who rebukes a man will later find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.
units.rightText: He that rebuketh a man shall afterward find more favor Than he that flattereth with the tongue.

units.leftText: He who robs his father or mother, saying, “It is not wrong,” is a companion to the man who destroys.
units.rightText: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression, The same is the companion of a destroyer.

units.leftText: A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.
units.rightText: He that is of a greedy spirit stirreth up strife; But he that putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be made fat.

units.leftText: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but one who walks in wisdom will be safe.
units.rightText: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; But whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.

units.leftText: Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but he who hides his eyes will receive many curses.
units.rightText: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack; But he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.

units.leftText: When the wicked come to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
units.rightText: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.

units.leftText: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.
units.rightText: He that being often reproved hardeneth his neck Shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

units.leftText: When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
units.rightText: When the righteous are increased, the people rejoice; But when a wicked man beareth rule, the people sigh.

units.leftText: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
units.rightText: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father; But he that keepeth company with harlots wasteth his substance.

units.leftText: By justice a king brings stability to the land, but a man who exacts tribute demolishes it.
units.rightText: The king by justice establisheth the land; But he that exacteth gifts overthroweth it.
leftNotes: 29:4 Or who taxes heavily or who takes bribes

units.leftText: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
units.rightText: A man that flattereth his neighbor Spreadeth a net for his steps.

units.leftText: An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.
units.rightText: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare; But the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

units.leftText: The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.
units.rightText: The righteous taketh knowledge of the cause of the poor; The wicked hath not understanding to know it.

units.leftText: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
units.rightText: Scoffers set a city in a flame; But wise men turn away wrath.

units.leftText: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.
units.rightText: If a wise man hath a controversy with a foolish man, Whether he be angry or laugh, there will be no rest.

units.leftText: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.
units.rightText: The bloodthirsty hate him that is perfect; And as for the upright, they seek his life.
leftNotes: 29:10 Or but the upright seek his soul

units.leftText: A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.
units.rightText: A fool uttereth all his anger; But a wise man keepeth it back and stilleth it.

units.leftText: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.
units.rightText: If a ruler hearkeneth to falsehood, All his servants are wicked.

units.leftText: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
units.rightText: The poor man and the oppressor meet together; Jehovah lighteneth the eyes of them both.

units.leftText: A king who judges the poor with fairness— his throne will be established forever.
units.rightText: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, His throne shall be established for ever.

units.leftText: A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
units.rightText: The rod and reproof give wisdom; But a child left to himself causeth shame to his mother.

units.leftText: When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
units.rightText: When the wicked are increased, transgression increaseth; But the righteous shall look upon their fall.

units.leftText: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
units.rightText: Correct thy son, and he will give thee rest; Yea, he will give delight unto thy soul.

units.leftText: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law.
units.rightText: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; But he that keepeth the law, happy is he.

units.leftText: A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
units.rightText: A servant will not be corrected by words; For though he understand, he will not give heed.

units.leftText: Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
units.rightText: Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? There is more hope of a fool than of him.

units.leftText: A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.
units.rightText: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child Shall have him become a son at the last.

units.leftText: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.
units.rightText: An angry man stirreth up strife, And a wrathful man aboundeth in transgression.

units.leftText: A man’s pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.
units.rightText: A man’s pride shall bring him low; But he that is of a lowly spirit shall obtain honor.

units.leftText: A partner to a thief hates his own soul; he receives the oath but does not testify.
units.rightText: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul; He heareth the adjuration and uttereth nothing.

units.leftText: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
units.rightText: The fear of man bringeth a snare; But whoso putteth his trust in Jehovah shall be safe.

units.leftText: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.
units.rightText: Many seek the ruler’s favor; But a man’s judgment cometh from Jehovah.

units.leftText: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
units.rightText: An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous; And he that is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.

units.leftText: These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh — the burden that this man declared to Ithiel: “I am weary, O God, and worn out.
units.rightText: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh; the oracle. The man saith unto Ithiel, unto Ithiel and Ucal:
leftNotes: 30:1 Or declared to Ithiel: “I am weary, O God, but I can prevail. (revocalizations); Hebrew declared to Ithiel—to Ithiel and Ucal:

units.leftText: Surely I am the most ignorant of men, and I lack the understanding of a man.
units.rightText: Surely I am more brutish than any man, And have not the understanding of a man;

units.leftText: I have not learned wisdom, and I have no knowledge of the Holy One.
units.rightText: And I have not learned wisdom, Neither have I the knowledge of the Holy One.

units.leftText: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son— surely you know!
units.rightText: Who hath ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who hath gathered the wind in his fists? Who hath bound the waters in his garment? Who hath established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if thou knowest?

units.leftText: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
units.rightText: Every word of God is tried: He is a shield unto them that take refuge in him.

units.leftText: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.
units.rightText: Add thou not unto his words, Lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.

units.leftText: Two things I ask of You — do not refuse me before I die:
units.rightText: Two things have I asked of thee; Deny me them not before I die:

units.leftText: Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread that is my portion.
units.rightText: Remove far from me falsehood and lies; Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is needful for me:

units.leftText: Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.
units.rightText: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is Jehovah? Or lest I be poor, and steal, And use profanely the name of my God.

units.leftText: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.
units.rightText: Slander not a servant unto his master, Lest he curse thee, and thou be held guilty.

units.leftText: There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
units.rightText: There is a generation that curse their father, And bless not their mother.

units.leftText: There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyes and yet unwashed of their filth.
units.rightText: There is a generation that are pure in their own eyes, And yet are not washed from their filthiness.

units.leftText: There is a generation— how haughty are their eyes and pretentious are their glances —
units.rightText: There is a generation, oh how lofty are their eyes! And their eyelids are lifted up.

units.leftText: there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.
units.rightText: There is a generation whose teeth are as swords, and their jaw teeth as knives, To devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from among men.

units.leftText: The leech has two daughters: Give and Give. There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’:
units.rightText: The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give. There are three things that are never satisfied, Yea, four that say not, Enough:

units.leftText: Sheol, the barren womb, land never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
units.rightText: Sheol; and the barren womb; The earth that is not satisfied with water; And the fire that saith not, Enough.

units.leftText: As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.
units.rightText: The eye that mocketh at his father, And despiseth to obey his mother, The ravens of the valley shall pick it out, And the young eagles shall eat it.

units.leftText: There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I cannot understand:
units.rightText: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Yea, four which I know not:

units.leftText: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship at sea, and the way of a man with a maiden.
units.rightText: The way of an eagle in the air; The way of a serpent upon a rock; The way of a ship in the midst of the sea; And the way of a man with a maiden.

units.leftText: This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
units.rightText: So is the way of an adulterous woman; She eateth, and wipeth her mouth, And saith, I have done no wickedness.

units.leftText: Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
units.rightText: For three things the earth doth tremble, And for four, which it cannot bear:

units.leftText: a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food,
units.rightText: For a servant when he is king; And a fool when he is filled with food;

units.leftText: an unloved woman who marries, and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.
units.rightText: For an odious woman when she is married; And a handmaid that is heir to her mistress.

units.leftText: Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise:
units.rightText: There are four things which are little upon the earth, But they are exceeding wise:

units.leftText: The ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;
units.rightText: The ants are a people not strong, Yet they provide their food in the summer;

units.leftText: the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
units.rightText: The conies are but a feeble folk, Yet make they their houses in the rocks;
leftNotes: 30:26 Or the coneys or the hyraxes

units.leftText: the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation;
units.rightText: The locusts have no king, Yet go they forth all of them by bands;

units.leftText: and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.
units.rightText: The lizard taketh hold with her hands, Yet is she in kings’ palaces.

units.leftText: There are three things that are stately in their stride, and four that are impressive in their walk:
units.rightText: There are three things which are stately in their march, Yea, four which are stately in going:

units.leftText: a lion, mighty among beasts, refusing to retreat before anything;
units.rightText: The lion, which is mightiest among beasts, And turneth not away for any;

units.leftText: a strutting rooster; a he-goat; and a king with his army around him.
units.rightText: The greyhound; the he-goat also; And the king against whom there is no rising up.
leftNotes: 30:31 Or a king against whom there is no rising up

units.leftText: If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil, put your hand over your mouth.
units.rightText: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, Or if thou hast thought evil, Lay thy hand upon thy mouth.

units.leftText: For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood, so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”
units.rightText: For the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, And the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood; So the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.

units.leftText: These are the words of King Lemuel — the burden that his mother taught him:
units.rightText: The words of king Lemuel; the oracle which his mother taught him.

units.leftText: What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb? What, O son of my vows?
units.rightText: What, my son? and what, O son of my womb? And what, O son of my vows?
leftNotes: 31:2 Or What or What are you doing

units.leftText: Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings.
units.rightText: Give not thy strength unto women, Nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.

units.leftText: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, or for rulers to crave strong drink,
units.rightText: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes to say, Where is strong drink?

units.leftText: lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice.
units.rightText: Lest they drink, and forget the law, And pervert the justice due to any that is afflicted.

units.leftText: Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.
units.rightText: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, And wine unto the bitter in soul:

units.leftText: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
units.rightText: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, And remember his misery no more.

units.leftText: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.
units.rightText: Open thy mouth for the dumb, In the cause of all such as are left desolate.

units.leftText: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy. The Virtues of a Noble Woman
units.rightText: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, And minister justice to the poor and needy.

units.leftText: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
units.rightText: A worthy woman who can find? For her price is far above rubies.
leftNotes: 31:10 Verses 10–31 are an acrostic poem, each verse beginning with the successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

units.leftText: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.
units.rightText: The heart of her husband trusteth in her, And he shall have no lack of gain.

units.leftText: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.
units.rightText: She doeth him good and not evil All the days of her life.

units.leftText: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.
units.rightText: She seeketh wool and flax, And worketh willingly with her hands.

units.leftText: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.
units.rightText: She is like the merchant-ships; She bringeth her bread from afar.

units.leftText: She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household and portions for her maidservants.
units.rightText: She riseth also while it is yet night, And giveth food to her household, And their task to her maidens.

units.leftText: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
units.rightText: She considereth a field, and buyeth it; With the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.

units.leftText: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.
units.rightText: She girdeth her loins with strength, And maketh strong her arms.
leftNotes: 31:17 Hebrew She girds her loins

units.leftText: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
units.rightText: She perceiveth that her merchandise is profitable; Her lamp goeth not out by night.

units.leftText: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.
units.rightText: She layeth her hands to the distaff, And her hands hold the spindle.

units.leftText: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
units.rightText: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; Yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.

units.leftText: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
units.rightText: She is not afraid of the snow for her household; For all her household are clothed with scarlet.
leftNotes: 31:21 Or doubly clothed

units.leftText: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
units.rightText: She maketh for herself carpets of tapestry; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.

units.leftText: Her husband is known at the city gates, where he sits among the elders of the land.
units.rightText: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sitteth among the elders of the land.

units.leftText: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.
units.rightText: She maketh linen garments and selleth them, And delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

units.leftText: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
units.rightText: Strength and dignity are her clothing; And she laugheth at the time to come.

units.leftText: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
units.rightText: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; And the law of kindness is on her tongue.

units.leftText: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
units.rightText: She looketh well to the ways of her household, And eateth not the bread of idleness.

units.leftText: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:
units.rightText: Her children rise up, and call her blessed; Her husband also, and he praiseth her, saying:

units.leftText: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”
units.rightText: Many daughters have done worthily, But thou excellest them all.

units.leftText: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
units.rightText: Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman that feareth Jehovah, she shall be praised.

units.leftText: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
units.rightText: Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.
